  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">We continue to believe that Tilray remains uniquely positioned to maintain and gain significant market share in the markets in which we participate. We benefit from our end-to-end vertically-integrated infrastructure and well-placed investments, which are comprised of two EU-GMP cultivation facilities located in Portugal and Germany; our fully owned route-to-market encompassing sales, marketing and distribution infrastructure in Germany&#160;and Italy; a network of leading distributors who we work with in the various other countries in which we operate; and, our extensive genetics portfolio and demonstrated commitment and expertise related to the cultivation and production of high-quality, safe cannabis products.&#160; Tilray&#8217;s International business also benefits from the depth and breadth of knowledge, experience, relationships and infrastructure we have transferred from our leading participation and investment in&#160;the Canadian medical and adult-use markets. We believe that these assets and attributes, combined with our ability to navigate complex regulatory environments, will continue to drive our leadership in international medical markets and allow us to successfully enter new markets as they adopt medical cannabis and potentially adult-use regulations and may also serve to support a potential U.S. participation in the event of federal legalization.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Germany</i>. Today, Germany remains the largest medical cannabis market in Europe.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">On April 1, 2024, the Cannabis Act, consisting of two parts, the CanG and MedCanG, was signed into law by the Office of the Federal President and decriminalization and MedCanG portions of the Cannabis Act became effective. The MedCanG provides for several important medical cannabis reforms including the reclassification of medical cannabis from a narcotic to non-narcotic and the abolishment of the tender for domestic production, which has been replaced with a regular licensing scheme under the authority of the Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices (the &#8220;BfArM&#8221;). Three licenses for domestic cultivation have been issued, with Tilray receiving the first one. The foreseen enhanced accessibility to medical cannabis due to non-narcotic prescriptions has had the desired effect. The prescription numbers have risen since April 1, 2024 and, accordingly, we have seen a significant increase in our business in Germany where we supply the market with a wide range of medical cannabis extracts and whole flower. In addition, the Federal Joint Committee (the &#8220;G-BA&#8221;) which issues directives for the German health insurance funds, enacted a resolution in July 2024 allowing for a significant reduction of reservation of approval. This is expected to have a positive market effect, allowing more doctors and specialists to be able to prescribe medical cannabis without receiving prior approval from statutory insurers. Tilray is well positioned to benefit from this change given our leading market share within the medical cannabis extracts segment that tends to have high levels of insurance coverage.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We continue to believe that Tilray is well-positioned in Germany, especially since&#160;the enactment of MedCanG benefits our medical leadership in the German market and given that we are one of only three cultivators of medical cannabis in Germany as our wholly owned subsidiary, Aphria RX, was awarded the first&#160;license for the cultivation of medical cannabis in Germany by the BfArM under the liberalized regime. We believe that this license will improve our ability to meet the needs of patients and provide cannabis of the utmost quality and enhanced availability to a broader market.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We continue to see increased differentiation between the physician-led and the patient-led channels.&#160; In response, we have launched the Tilray Craft, Broken Coast, Redecan and Good Supply brands and related medical cannabis products, which provides the patient with a segmented portfolio of products while we continue to deliver on the trust, safety and consistency that has become expected from our Tilray Medical brand.</p>
  <p style="margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Poland</i>.&#160; In Poland, cannabis was legalized for medical use in 2018 and&#160;is prescribed to patients by a physician and dispensed by pharmacies.&#160;Today, all doctors in Poland are allowed to prescribe medical cannabis and it is a self-pay&#160;market as medical cannabis is not reimbursed by the Polish health service. In November 2024, Poland implemented strict restrictions on telemedicine, which have significantly impacted the growth of the market with prescription numbers decreasing from 68,000 in October 2024 to 28,000 in December 2024. Tilray is a leading supplier of medical cannabis in Poland through our network of distributor partnerships.&#160;We predominantly supply the market with whole flower medical cannabis products.&#160; &#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>United Kingdom</i>.&#160; Since November 2018, doctors in the UK have been able to prescribe medical cannabis for medicinal use for patients with medical conditions that had failed to respond to first-line medications.&#160; The market today is predominantly all self-pay and prescriptions are facilitated by private clinics.&#160; Today, we supply the UK market with mainly whole flower products through our distributor partners.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Ireland</i>.&#160;In June 2019, the Minister for Health signed legislation allowing for the operation of the Medical Cannabis Access Programme (&#8220;MCAP&#8221;) on a pilot basis for five years. The MCAP allows a medical consultant to prescribe a cannabis-based treatment for a narrow set of specified medical conditions, where the patient has failed to respond to standard treatment. Reimbursement is available for products which have received the appropriate approval. Tilray was one of the first players to enter the Irish market and is one of a few suppliers which has received approval for its products to be prescribed and to have been granted reimbursement status. Today, we supply our approved extract product to Ireland through our distribution partner.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Italy</i>. In May 2023, FL Group, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Tilray received authorization from Italy&#8217;s Ministry of Health to distribute three new medical cannabis compounds to pharmacies across Italy.&#160;With FL Group, we have an established broad national pharmaceutical distribution network in Italy, where medical cannabis is prescribed by doctors and reimbursed by the healthcare system to eligible patients.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Australia</i>. In 2016, the Australian Government legalized medicinal cannabis, which is regulated by the Therapeutic Goods Administration.&#160; Medical cannabis is prescribed by a doctor but there is no coverage under the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme.&#160; Tilray Medical suppliers the market with wide portfolio of medical cannabis extracts as well as whole flower products.&#160; We see increased differentiation between the physician-led and the patient-led channels.&#160; In response, we launched the Broken Coast, Redecan and Good Supply brands and products, which provide&#160;the patient with a segmented portfolio of products while we continue to deliver on the trust, safety and consistency that has become expected from our Tilray Medical brand.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 9pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Wellness market trends.</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Tilray Wellness&#8217;s branded business continues to grow across brick-and-mortar retail as well as ecommerce, further establishing its leading market share position in better for you categories.&#160;The Company continues to focus on value-added innovation within the wellness space&#160;with the launch of branded Whole Flaxseed and Ground Flaxseed and Superseed Snack Clusters in partnership with Whole Foods Market as well as continued emphasis on The Humble Seed, a seed-forward cracker brand which was purchased&#160;earlier this year.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Acquisitions, Strategic Transactions and Synergies</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">We strive to continue to expand our business, on a consolidated basis, through a combination of organic growth and acquisition. While we continue to execute against our strategic initiatives that we believe will result in&#160;long-term, sustainable growth and value to our stockholders, we continue to evaluate potential acquisitions and other strategic transactions of businesses that we believe complement our existing portfolio, infrastructure and capabilities or provide us with the opportunity to enter attractive new geographic markets and product categories as well as expand our existing capabilities. In addition, we have exited certain businesses and continue to evaluate certain businesses within our portfolio that are dilutive to profitability and cash flow. As a result, we incur transaction costs in connection with identifying and completing acquisitions and strategic transactions, as well as ongoing integration and restructuring costs as we combine acquired companies and continue to achieve synergies, which is offset by income generated in connection with the execution of these transactions. For the year&#160;ended May 31, 2025, we incurred&#160;$4.5&#160;million of transaction costs (income), net,&#160;as discussed further below.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Effective&#160;September 1, 2024,&#160;Tilray acquired Craft Acquisition II a portfolio of&#160;four craft brands and breweries comprised of Atwater Brewery,&#160;Hop Valley Brewing Company,&#160;Terrapin Beer Co., and&#160;Revolver Brewing&#160;from Molson, see Note 9&#160;(Business Acquisition). We expect this acquisition to further&#160;the execution of our beverage strategy, which we believe&#160;will have positive impacts on our&#160;beverage segment leading to increased revenues and whitespace penetration.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <div class="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
   <div class="PGFTR" style="text-align: center; width: 100%">
    <div class="hf-row">
     <div class="hf-cell PGNUM" style="text-align: center; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times New Roman;">
      45
     </div>

   <div class="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%">
    <div class="hf-row">

      &#160;

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i><b>Beverage segment Project 420:</b>&#160;</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">In November 2020, we entered the beverage category with the acquisition of SweetWater Brewing Company, one of the largest independent craft brewers in the U.S. by volume, with the vision of creating a larger and more diversified global lifestyle consumer products company.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">This initial acquisition provided us with a foundation to pursue additional acquisitions in the beverage category and scale our business on a national basis. We acquired Alpine Beer Company, Green Flash and Breckenridge Distillery in December 2021, Montauk Brewing Company in November 2022, Craft Acquisition I in October 2023 and Craft Acquisition II in September 2024.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">With Craft Acquisition I and Craft Acquisition II, we capitalized on opportunities to acquire additional beverage businesses that consisted of strong brands in decline and in need of investment in order to promote growth at a significantly reduced price. To support the growth of these acquired brands and establish a clear path to profitability, we implemented Project 420, which is a comprehensive plan covering (i) SKU rationalization; (ii) Geographic rationalization; (iii) Distributor rationalization; and&#160;(iv) synergy optimization plan through which we expect to invest in the acquired brands for growth and improve profitability:</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;">
   <tbody>
    <tr>
     <td style="vertical-align:top;width:2.5%;">&#160;</td>
     <td style="vertical-align:top;width:1.7%;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">-</p> </td>
     <td style="vertical-align: top; width: auto; text-align: justify;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">SKU rationalization</span></i>&#160;&#8211;&#160;In response to the declining growth in the craft beer industry and consolidation of distributors, we are working with our distributors in various markets to streamline our portfolio by eliminating duplicative and slower growth products, which had the immediate effect of reducing revenue. However, by eliminating these slower growing SKUs, we are able to focus our attention and resources on our higher growth SKUs and the introduction of new innovation, which we expect will accelerate our revenue growth in future quarters. Going forward, we will continue to manage SKU performance within our portfolio on a &#8220;one in and one out basis&#8221;&#160;to maximize SKU productivity.</td>
    </tr>

   </tbody>
  </table>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;">
   <tbody>
    <tr>
     <td style="vertical-align:top;width:2.5%;">&#160;</td>
     <td style="vertical-align:top;width:1.7%;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">-</p> </td>
     <td style="vertical-align: top; width: auto; text-align: justify;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Geographic rationalization</span></i><i> </i>&#8211;<i> </i>Our brands generate sales in all states however, their results are significantly stronger in their home markets.&#160;For example, SweetWater is located in Georgia and, as a result, its revenues are stronger in Georgia, Alabama, North Carolina and Florida, while 10 Barrel, which is located &#160;in Oregon has stronger revenue in Oregon, Washington, Idaho and Wyoming.&#160;In away markets, like Oregon for SweetWater, and Georgia for 10 Barrel, the brands are not as strong in the away states.&#160;Our geographic rationalization works to concentrate our efforts in individual states with our strongest brands in those states.&#160;As we reduce the distribution of away markets brands in those states, we are working to increase the distribution and shelf space of home market brands.&#160;This initiative is consistent with our Regional Jewel strategy developed in conjunction with the Boston Consulting Group.</td>
    </tr>

   </tbody>
  </table>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;">
   <tbody>
    <tr>
     <td style="vertical-align:top;width:2.5%;">&#160;</td>
     <td style="vertical-align:top;width:1.7%;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">-</p> </td>
     <td style="vertical-align: top; width: auto; text-align: justify;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Distributor rationalization</span></i><i> </i>&#8211;<i> </i>As a result of our various acquisitions in the last five years, we have over 750 distributors and 975 distributor shipping locations. As a result, we are shipping to multiple distributors in the same geography as well as splitting the allocation of local brands between multiple distributors. The goal of the distributor rationalization is to reduce our distributor footprint down to between 450 and 500 distributors concentrating those distributor&#8217;s effort on our brands and SKUs, while minimizing logistical complexities.</td>
    </tr>

   </tbody>
  </table>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;">
   <tbody>
    <tr>
     <td style="vertical-align:top;width:2.5%;">&#160;</td>
     <td style="vertical-align:top;width:1.7%;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">-</p> </td>
     <td style="vertical-align: top; width: auto; text-align: justify;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Synergy optimization plan</span></i><i> </i>&#8211;<i> </i>We previously announced a $25&#160;million synergy plan focused on optimizing our production footprint and eliminating redundancies in manufacturing and warehouse assets.&#160;By integrating the newly acquired facilities into our existing footprint, we are optimizing capacities, utilization and better absorbing fixed overheads. This in turn is improving our gross margins.&#160;During the year, we increased the synergy plan by $8 million to $33 million and have achieved $24.1 million of those savings to date.&#160;We expect to complete the synergy optimization plan in the third&#160;quarter of fiscal 2026.</td>
    </tr>

   </tbody>
  </table>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;">
   <tbody>
    <tr>
     <td style="vertical-align:top;width:2.5%;">&#160;</td>
     <td style="vertical-align:top;width:1.7%;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">-</p> </td>
     <td style="vertical-align: top; width: auto; text-align: justify;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Brand and</span></i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#160;</span><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">business investment</span></i>&#160;&#8211;<i> </i>We have been and are continuing to increase our investment in the marketing, promotion and infrastructure of our recently acquired brands in order to reestablish their dominance in their core markets. Our intention is to fund this investment through the cost savings and synergies achieved through Project 420.&#160;&#160;</td>
    </tr>

   </tbody>
  </table>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">For the year ended May 31, 2025, our SKU and geographic rationalization resulted in a reduction in net sales of approximately $20&#160;million. We believe this temporary reduction will be offset by the growth of our new product innovation, including in new beverage categories, and brand extensions during&#160;the near term future. This revenue reduction has a corresponding decrease in our Adjusted EBITDA for the year ended&#160;May 31, 2025, of $6.0&#160;million.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">It is important to note, however, that there is a lag between the discontinuation of the SKUs and the associated reduction in revenue, which has an immediate effect, and the acceleration of the growth of our existing SKUs and the introduction of new innovation and the associated increase in revenue, which takes time due to retailer resets.&#160;We also expect these efforts will lead to improved sales and margins, with benefits realized through lower selling costs, as well as reduced requirements for working capital through inventory reductions and an improvement in our cash conversion cycle.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Political and Economic Environment</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Our results of operations may continue to be affected by economic, political, legislative, regulatory, legal actions, global volatility and general market disruption resulting from&#160;geopolitical tensions, such as Russia's continued incursion into Ukraine,&#160;the ongoing events in the Middle East and political uncertainty in certain countries in Europe. Economic conditions, such as recessionary trends, inflation, supply chain disruptions, interest and monetary exchange rates, government fiscal policies, and the recent economic uncertainties resulting from&#160;certain changes in U.S. global economic policy, including changes on global trade policies can have a significant effect on operations. More specifically, there are no expected impacts on revenue from the recently enacted U.S. tariffs and foreign enacted retaliatory&#160;tariffs (&#8220;Tariffs&#8221;). From a cost perspective, we believe the recently enacted tariffs could impact input materials such as aluminum, hops, barley, malt and vape componentry&#160;which are partially imported&#160;but we intend to mitigate these impacts to the extent&#160;possible.</p>

These non-GAAP financial measures reflect an additional way of viewing aspects of operations that, when viewed with U.S. GAAP results, provide a more complete understanding of the business. The Company strongly encourages investors and shareholders to review Company financial statements and publicly filed reports in their entirety and not to rely on any single financial measure. Please see &#8220;Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures to GAAP Measures&#8221; below for a reconciliation of such non-GAAP Measures to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures, as well as a discussion of our adjusted gross margin, adjusted gross profit and adjusted EBITDA measures and the calculation of such measures.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:25pt;"><i>Constant Currency Presentation</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">We believe that this measure provides useful information to investors because it provides transparency to underlying performance in our consolidated net sales by excluding the effect that foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations have on period-to-period comparability given the volatility in foreign currency exchange markets. To present this information for historical periods, current period net sales for entities reporting in currencies other than the U.S. Dollar are translated into U.S. Dollars at the average monthly exchange rates in effect during the corresponding period of the prior fiscal year rather than at the actual average monthly exchange rate in effect during the current period of the current fiscal year. As a result, the foreign currency impact is equal to the current year&#8217;s results in local currencies multiplied by the change in average foreign currency exchange rate between the current fiscal period and the corresponding period of the prior fiscal year.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

The Company&#8217;s management believes that this presentation provides useful information to management, analysts and investors regarding certain additional financial and business trends relating to its short-term liquidity position by combing these two GAAP metrics.</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt;"><i><b>Beverage revenue </b></i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Net revenue from our Beverage operations&#160;increased&#160;to $240.6&#160;million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, compared to net revenue of&#160;$202.1&#160;million for the prior fiscal year ended May 31, 2024. The increase&#160;in beverage revenue was primarily driven by our newly launched innovation in the HD-D9 product category and our Craft Acquisition II, which was effective as of September 1, 2024, and included the brands and breweries of Hop Valley Brewing Company, Terrapin Beer Company, Revolver Brewing, and Atwater Brewery. Further, the prior fiscal year period did not reflect a full period of revenue from Craft Acquisition I, which was completed on September 29, 2023. These&#160;impacts to beverage revenue were offset&#160;by&#160;the SKU rationalization implemented in connection with Project 420, which resulted in a&#160;reduction of net revenue by approximately&#160;$20&#160;million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025.&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Revenue from medical cannabis:</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Gross revenue from Canadian medical cannabis&#160;decreased 1%&#160;to&#160;$25.0 million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025<b><i>,</i></b> compared to gross revenue of $25.2 million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2024. On a constant currency basis, gross&#160;revenue from Canadian medical cannabis&#160;increased to&#160;$25.8 million from $25.2 million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025. This increase in gross revenue from medical cannabis on a constant currency basis was primarily driven by growth in the insured patient&#160;category exceeding the decline in uninsured patient&#160;attrition to the&#160;adult-use recreational market.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Revenue from adult-use cannabis: </i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">During the fiscal year ended&#160;May 31, 2025&#160;our gross revenue from Canadian adult-use cannabis product&#160;decreased&#160;16% to&#160;$224.0 million compared to revenue of $266.8 million for the prior fiscal year.&#160;On a constant currency basis,&#160;our gross revenue from Canadian adult-use cannabis&#160;decreased&#160;13% to $231.0 million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025.&#160;The decrease in gross adult-use revenue was driven by our renewed focus on preserving gross margin and maintaining a higher average selling price in growing categories&#160;such as vapes that have experienced a high degree of price compression. At the end of the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, we began increasing&#160;our participation&#160;in these categories as a result of our capex investments to improve these trends in the near term future. Additionally, we have shifted our&#160;strategic&#160;focus to redirect 7.2&#160;million grams&#160;of cannabis to&#160;international cannabis markets to take advantage of the higher margin sales available&#160;in these markets. While some of these products were sold during the fourth fiscal quarter, some inventories were&#160;deferred to&#160;fiscal year 2026. The resulting impact of this strategic decision&#160;caused a temporary decline in gross adult-use cannabis revenue and cannabis revenue overall until&#160;their eventual sale. We intend to enhance our global supply chain through Phase II of our accelerated growth plan and increase our cultivation footprint to support the&#160;growing demand in both the Canadian and international markets. Lastly, gross revenue from Canadian adult-use cannabis products also included $1.5&#160;million of cannabis advisory services revenue in the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, compared to $1.5 million in the fiscal year ended May 31, 2024.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Wholesale cannabis revenue:&#160;</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Gross revenue from wholesale cannabis&#160;decreased to&#160;$18.2 million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, compared to revenue of&#160;$25.3 million for the prior fiscal year ended May 31, 2024.&#160;On a constant currency basis, gross revenue from wholesale cannabis for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025 was $18.8 million&#160;compared to $25.3 million for the prior fiscal year ended May 31, 2024. Due to the transition to asset-light business models, the Canadian cannabis industry has experienced a reduction in excess inventory resulting in price increases in the B2B market. This shift in market dynamics and demand enabled us to strategically&#160;sell inventory that was sought after&#160;in the wholesale market&#160;during the fiscal year but does not meet the high standards required for our branded product. In the near-term, we anticipate continued volatility and fluctuation in the wholesale market, and we will assess market conditions on a quarterly basis. Specifically, during the fourth quarter market&#160;conditions were less favorable and as a result&#160;we did not participate in the same volume of transactions when compared to the prior year fourth quarter.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>International cannabis revenue:</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Net revenue from international cannabis&#160;increased&#160;19% to&#160;$63.4 million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, compared to net revenue of&#160;$53.3 million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2024. On a constant currency&#160;basis, net revenue from international cannabis&#160;increased&#160;19% to&#160;$63.2 million, compared to the prior year period.&#160;The increase during the fiscal year was primarily driven by higher sales in Germany, attributed to the expanding German medical market where we maintained our leadership position in the reimbursed market and increased our sales in the self-pay market.&#160;This growth was partially offset by lower revenue in Poland when compared to the prior year period driven by the delay in the receipt of export/import permits and lower prescriptions due to restrictions placed on telemedicine in November 2024 as well as lower revenue in Australia and the strategic decision to exit the New Zealand medical market. International cannabis net revenue may fluctuate from quarter to quarter based upon the timing of the receipt of export/import permits as well as the timing of shipments from one quarter to the next. In the fourth quarter, we experienced extensive delays in the receipt of export permits from the Portugal authorities resulting in approximately 2.1 million grams of medical cannabis flowers that we had expected to ship to other markets instead of remaining in Portugal.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Distribution revenue </b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Net revenue from Distribution operations increased 5% to&#160;$271.2 million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, compared to net revenue of&#160;$258.7 million for the prior fiscal year&#160;ended May&#160;31, 2024. On a constant currency basis, given the change in&#160;the Euro and Argentine Peso against the U.S. Dollar during the fiscal year, net revenue from Distribution was&#160;$277.2&#160;million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, when compared to prior year&#160;period. The increase in distribution revenue, on a constant currency basis, for the fiscal year&#160;was driven by a change in product&#160;mix.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Wellness revenue </b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Our Wellness net revenue&#160;increased&#160;to&#160;$60.5&#160;million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025 compared to&#160;$55.3&#160;million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2024. On a constant currency basis for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, Wellness net revenue&#160;increased to&#160;$61.4&#160;million from&#160;$55.3&#160;million. The increase in net revenue was primarily&#160;attributed to our strategic focus on expanding our product range,&#160;including the relaunch&#160;of&#160;HiBall energy drinks and organic growth within our branded hemp food business&#160;related to higher consumption.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Adjusted Gross Profit and Adjusted Gross Margin</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Adjusted gross profit and adjusted gross margin are non-GAAP financial measures and may not be comparable to similar measures presented by other companies.&#160; Adjusted gross profit is our Gross profit (adjusted to exclude inventory valuation adjustment and purchase price accounting valuation step-up) and adjusted gross margin is our Gross margin (adjusted to exclude inventory valuation adjustment and purchase price accounting valuation step-up) and are both non-GAAP financial measures. The Company&#8217;s management believes that adjusted gross profit and adjusted gross margin are useful to our management to evaluate our business and operations, measure our performance, identify trends affecting our business, project our future performance, and make strategic decisions without the impacts of the aforementioned adjusted items.&#160; We do not consider adjusted gross profit and adjusted gross margin percentage in isolation or as an alternative to financial measures determined in accordance with GAAP.</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i>Beverage&#160;gross margin:</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Gross margin of&#160;39%&#160;for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025&#160;decreased from&#160;44%&#160;when compared to the fiscal year ended May 31,&#160;2024.&#160;Adjusted gross margin of&#160;39%&#160;decreased in the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, from&#160;46% in the fiscal year ended May 31,&#160;2024.&#160;The change in the adjusted beverage&#160;gross margin during the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025&#160;was driven by several factors, including&#160;our continued integration efforts of&#160;our Craft Acquisition I.&#160;The increased utilization of our facilities and improvements in our product&#160;mix as part of our strategic initiatives under Project 420 had favorable impacts on our adjusted gross margin,&#160;however, these improvements were more than offset by the impacts from the Craft Acquisition II, which has&#160;lower margins than our existing business.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i>Cannabis gross margin:</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Gross margin increased during the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025&#160;to&#160;40%&#160;from&#160;33% when compared to the fiscal year ended May 31,&#160;2024. Adjusted gross margin&#160;during the fiscal year&#160;ended May 31, 2025, increased to&#160;40%&#160;from&#160;36% when&#160;compared to the prior fiscal year ended May 31,&#160;2024.&#160;The improvement&#160;in gross margin and adjusted gross margin for the year ended May 31, 2025 was driven by our increased international cannabis revenue as a proportion of total cannabis revenue, which has higher margins than our Canadian cannabis business, as well as a continued focus in our Canadian cannabis business on maintaining a higher average selling price and&#160;favorable&#160;product mix to improve gross margins.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i>Distribution gross margin:</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Gross margin of&#160;11%&#160;for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025&#160;remained consistent when compared to the fiscal year ended&#160;May 31,&#160;2024, despite shortages in key pharmaceutical product lines as well as price reductions in certain key pharmaceutical lines of products.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i>Wellness gross margin:</i>&#160;&#160;</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Gross margin of 32% for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025&#160;increased from a gross margin of&#160;30%&#160;when compared to the fiscal year ended May 31,&#160;2024, resulting from strong operational efficiencies, lower input costs and&#160;the culmination of a change in sales mix towards&#160;higher margin product offerings including HiBall energy drinks.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

These costs&#160;increased by&#160;$2,125.2 million to $2,523.3 million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, compared to&#160;$398.1 million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2024. This increase was primarily a result of the non-cash impairments recorded in the period as described in detail below.&#160;Additionally, $20.1&#160;million of the increase year over year was attributed to&#160;the inclusion&#160;of expenses from our recent Craft Acquisition II, effective September 1, 2024, and that the prior year period did not reflect a full period of results from the Craft Acquisition I, which was completed on September 29, 2023. These changes, period over period, are described below.&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Salaries and wages&#160;increased by&#160;5%&#160;during the fiscal&#160;year ended May 31, 2025. The change&#160;was primarily due to&#160;the inclusion of&#160;employees from Craft Acquisition II, effective September 1, 2024, and the prior fiscal year period did not reflect a full period of results from Craft Acquisition I, completed on September 29, 2023. Additionally, included in&#160;the fiscal year ended&#160;May 31, 2025&#160;was $4.7&#160;million of retention payments that did not occur in the prior fiscal year period.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Office and general&#160;decreased by&#160;1% during the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025.&#160;The decrease&#160;was primarily due to the inclusion of deposit&#160;recoveries of $5.6 million compared to of&#160;bad debt recoveries of $4.4 million in the prior fiscal year period ended May 31, 2024. Further, we incurred&#160;expenses related to the Craft Acquisition II, effective September 1, 2024, and the prior fiscal year period ended May 31, 2024 did not reflect a full period of results from Craft Acquisition I due to the fact that it was completed on September 29, 2023. These impacts were partially offset by our continued cost saving initiatives.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company recognized stock-based compensation expense of&#160;$24.3 million for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025 compared to $31.8 million for the prior fiscal year period.&#160;Stock-based compensation expense&#160;is based on the&#160;time-based vesting schedules and varies according to the assumptions used in the vesting model. The decrease in stock-based compensation was driven by the vesting of previously issued stock options, restricted&#160;stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;) and stock appreciation rights (&#8220;SARs&#8221;) during the year ended May 31, 2025. Additionally, the decrease for the year ended May 31, 2025 was driven by the cancellation of certain performance-based RSUs.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Insurance expense&#160;decreased by&#160;6% for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025 to&#160;$11.8 million&#160;from $12.6&#160;million&#160;for&#160;the&#160;prior fiscal year period.&#160;The decrease in insurance expense for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025&#160;was driven by lower premiums on existing insurance policies, offset by premiums associated with new insurance policies that have been placed in connection with&#160;Craft Acquisition I and Craft Acquisition II.&#160; For the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025 as a percentage of revenue insurance was 1% compared to 2% in the prior fiscal year period, demonstrating our ability to manage our insurance policy cost&#160;despite growing the business.&#160;&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

Rent expense is predominantly comprised of&#160;operating lease expense&#160;for our brew pubs and office spaces.&#160;The decrease was driven by the exit from the Truss lease in the current fiscal year and a reduction in lease payments, which were&#160;previously included in the prior fiscal period results, offset by&#160;the expenses from&#160;Craft Acquisition II, effective September 1, 2024, and the prior fiscal year period did not reflect a full period of results from Craft Acquisition I due to the fact that it was completed on September 29, 2023.</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Selling costs</b></p>

These costs relate to third-party shipping costs for all segments, in addition to distributor commission incurred by the cannabis segment, Health Canada cannabis fees, and patient acquisition and maintenance costs. The&#160;increase&#160;for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025&#160;is predominately due to the higher freight costs experienced in the beverage segment.&#160;Additionally, during the year ended May 31, 2024, the Company received a&#160;refund of $3.3&#160;million related to&#160;cannabis selling fees related to an amended fee calculation and a commission refund that did not reoccur in the current fiscal period.</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Intangible asset impairments</i></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company performed the annual impairment test on its indefinite-life intangible assets, and for its finite-lived intangible assets, management assessed for asset specific indicators of impairment during the fourth quarter ended May 31, 2025, and based upon a combination of factors including a sustained decline in the Company&#8217;s market capitalization stemming from the uncertainty resulting from certain changes in U.S. global economic policy, including slower than anticipated progress in global cannabis legalization and overall declines in the craft beer industry sector, and a change in non-discretionary market inputs in the Company's discount rate,&#160;the Company recorded&#160;non-cash impairments&#160;of&#160;$334.2 million&#160;related to its finite-lived customer relationships &amp; distribution channel, $186.6 million related to its licenses, permits &amp; applications, which were considered indefinite-lived intangible assets and $327.1 million&#160;related to its finite-lived intellectual property, trademarks, knowhow &amp; brands. This impairment charge resulted in a corresponding income tax recovery of $121.4&#160;million, resulting in the corresponding reduction in deferred tax liabilities.&#160;In calculating the&#160;impairment charge, using an income approach, the Company&#160;used a discount rate of 10.00%-14.50%, a terminal growth rate of&#160;2%,&#160;and an average revenue growth rate of 5%-30% over&#160;5&#160;years to correlate with the cash flows anticipated with the individual intangible assets that were assessed.&#160;A reasonably possible change in any of the inputs within the determination of fair value would&#160;not&#160;result in a material change to the impairment recorded.</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">During the fiscal year ended May 31, 2024, there were&#160;no impairments to indefinite-lived intangible assets or finite-lived intangible assets.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Goodwill impairments</i></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">During the preceding quarter ended February 28, 2025, based upon a combination of factors including a sustained decline in the Company&#8217;s market capitalization stemming from the uncertainty resulting from certain changes in U.S. global economic policy, including slower than anticipated progress in global cannabis legalization and overall declines in the craft beer industry sector,&#160;the Company concluded that it is more likely than&#160;not,&#160;that the fair value of our reporting units were&#160;less than their carrying amounts as of&#160;February 28, 2025. Accordingly, the Company utilized the income approach, which uses future discounted cash flows, to determine the fair value of each reporting unit.&#160;As a result, the Company&#160;recorded non-cash impairment charges of&#160;$570.0 million&#160;of cannabis goodwill, $100.0 million&#160;of beverage goodwill,&#160;$25.0 million&#160;of wellness goodwill and $4.2 million&#160;of distribution goodwill for the nine&#160;months ended&#160;February 28, 2025.&#160;In the Company's cannabis goodwill assessment, the Company&#160;used a discount rate of&#160;12.00%,&#160;a terminal growth rate of&#160;5%, and an average revenue growth rate of&#160;34% over&#160;5&#160;years, based on an&#160;88% and&#160;40% average probability of&#160;anticipated EU and U.S. cannabis&#160;legalization, respectively and/or changes in drug policy in various countries within the next&#160;5&#160;years.&#160;In the Company's beverage goodwill assessment, the Company&#160;used a discount rate of&#160;9.25%, a terminal growth rate of&#160;2%,&#160;and an average revenue growth rate of&#160;12% over&#160;5&#160;years.&#160; In the Company's wellness goodwill assessment, the Company&#160;used a discount rate of&#160;10.50%, a terminal growth rate of&#160;2%,&#160;and an average revenue growth rate of&#160;7% over&#160;5&#160;years.&#160;In the Company's distribution&#160;goodwill assessment, the Company recorded $4,235&#160;of impairments, which brought the remaining distribution goodwill balance to&#160;$nil.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The Company then performed the annual impairment test during the fourth quarter ended May 31, 2025, and determined that through a combination of factors including a further decline in the Company's market capitalization, an increase in the discount rate, and changes to the aforementioned&#160;probabilities resulting&#160;from continued delays in&#160;legalization of cannabis within the United States and internationally, culminating&#160;in an unfavorable impact on the estimated future cash flows, and ultimately concluded that it is more likely than&#160;not,&#160;that the fair value of our reporting units were&#160;less than their carrying amounts as of May 31, 2025.&#160;Accordingly, the Company utilized the income approach, which uses future discounted cash flows, to determine the fair value of each reporting unit.&#160;As a result, the Company&#160;recorded additional non-cash impairment charges of&#160;$500.0 million&#160;of cannabis goodwill, $20.8 million&#160;of beverage goodwill and&#160;$28.2 million&#160;of wellness goodwill&#160;during the quarter&#160;ended May 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In the Company's cannabis goodwill assessment, the Company&#160;used a discount rate of&#160;14.50%,&#160;a terminal growth rate of&#160;5%, and an average revenue growth rate of&#160;34% over&#160;5&#160;years, based on an&#160;65% and 25% average probability of&#160;anticipated EU and U.S. cannabis&#160;legalization, respectively and/or changes in drug policy in various countries within the next&#160;5&#160;years. A&#160;1%&#160;increase in the discount rate would result in an additional $133.8 million in impairment, a&#160;1%&#160;decrease in the terminal growth rate would result in an additional $93.5 million&#160;in impairment,&#160;a&#160;5%&#160;decrease in the average growth rate would result in an additional $23.4 million&#160;in impairment, a&#160;5%&#160;decrease in the probability of EU cannabis legalization&#160;would result in an additional $44.0 million in impairment and a&#160;5%&#160;decrease in the probability of US cannabis legalization&#160;would result in an additional $17.1 million&#160;in impairment.&#160;Changes to those probabilities resulting in continued delays in or cessation of legalization of cannabis within the United States and internationally, or adverse regulatory changes to existing legislation, could have an unfavorable impact on the estimated future cash flows, and ultimately, the fair value of the cannabis reporting unit, which&#160;may&#160;result in a material impairment expense recognized in future reporting periods.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In the Company's beverage goodwill assessment, the Company&#160;used a discount rate of&#160;10.00%, a terminal growth rate of&#160;2%,&#160;and an average revenue growth rate of 2% over&#160;5&#160;years,&#160;which brought the remaining beverage goodwill balance to&#160;$nil.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In the Company's wellness goodwill assessment, the Company&#160;used a discount rate of&#160;12.25%, a terminal growth rate of&#160;2%,&#160;and an average revenue growth rate of&#160;7% over&#160;5&#160;years,&#160;which brought the remaining beverage goodwill balance to&#160;$nil.&#160;</p>
  <p style="margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 36pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">For the fiscal year ended May 31, 2024, the Company recognized $nil impairment expense.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: -9pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Other than temporary write-down of convertible notes receivable</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: -9pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">During the fiscal year&#160;ended May 31, 2025, the Company recognized an&#160;other-than-temporary change in fair value of convertible notes receivable, which resulted in a non-cash expense&#160;of&#160;$21.7 million compared to $42.7&#160;million for the prior fiscal year period related to the MedMen Convertible Note. The&#160;MedMen Convertible Note was valued based upon the estimated fair value of the&#160;collateral assets net of estimated disposal costs and has been reduced to reflect recent developments in restructuring efforts. See Note 11&#160;(Convertible notes receivable), for additional transactions related to the MedMen Convertible Note, which occurred during the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025.&#160;&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Litigation costs</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Litigation costs of $17.3&#160;million were expensed during the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025 compared&#160;$8.3&#160;million in the prior fiscal year.   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Restructuring costs </b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In connection with the execution of our acquisition strategy and strategic transactions, the Company incurred non-recurring restructuring and exit costs associated with the integration efforts of these transactions. In connection with these efforts, during the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, the Company incurred $34.3 million of restructuring charges&#160;compared to&#160;$15.6&#160;million for the prior fiscal year period.&#160;All restructuring&#160;plans are approved at the executive level, and their associated expenses are recognized in&#160;the fiscal period in which the plan is&#160;committed.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Within the Cannabis segment, our restructuring costs predominantly related to&#160;the&#160;HEXO acquisition, which were completed&#160;within 24 months from the&#160;acquisition, which occurred in June 2023. In the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, we&#160;recognized&#160;$10.4&#160;million of expenses related to employee termination severance and benefits and other costs related to&#160;the conversion of the HEXO Quebec cultivation facility from cannabis production&#160;to produce production,&#160;the optimization of our Redecan facilities, and&#160;$1.0 million of restructuring charges related to the exiting of the Truss facility following its sale to a third party in the fiscal year ended May 31, 2024. Additionally, the Company recognized $1.1 million of cost associated with the closure and sale of our Avanti facility, which occurred during the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025. The Company also recognized $2.1 million of exit&#160;cost in connection with the termination of its contract with its distribution partner in the Quebec adult-use cannabis market and the insourcing of the&#160;function.&#160;Lastly, the Company recognized $0.8&#160;million&#160;of restructuring charges related to our decision to exit the New Zealand medical cannabis market&#160;during the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Within the Beverage&#160;segment during the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, the Company recognized&#160;$1.6&#160;million&#160;of expenses related to employee&#160;severance and benefits and&#160;$4.2 million of costs associated with the consolidation&#160;of production sites&#160;through the integration of Craft Acquisition I and the Craft Acquisition II. Additionally,&#160;the Company recognized $8.5 million&#160;of restructuring&#160;charges related to the closure of the Hop Valley production facility, which was&#160;accrued, but not yet paid. Lastly, the Company recognized $1.6 million&#160;of restructuring charges related to terminating a legacy storage&#160;agreement from Craft Acquisition I. We expect to transition to a new storage facility in fiscal year&#160;2026, consistent with our&#160;announced cost savings initiatives.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Within the Distribution segment during the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, the Company recognized $0.5&#160;million&#160;of restructuring charges related to the divestiture of&#160;its retail pharmacy location in Argentina.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Lastly, for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, the Company recognized $2.5&#160;million&#160;of costs associated with the investment held in Superhero Acquisition Corp.&#160;as a result of MedMen&#8217;s ongoing restructuring and&#160;liquidation undertakings.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Transaction (income) costs, net</b></p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Transaction (income) costs, net, consists of acquisition related income and expenses, including&#160;legal fees, financial advisor and other third-party due diligence cost and expenses as well as any transaction related compensation. During the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025,&#160;transaction (income) costs, net&#160;decreased 71% from the prior fiscal year period as a result of lower transaction costs associated with Craft Acquisition II in the current fiscal year compared to the costs associated&#160;with the&#160;HEXO, Truss and the Craft Acquisition I in the prior fiscal year. &#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">For the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, the Company recognized a change in fair value of its convertible debentures payable of $nil&#160;compared to $19.7&#160;million in the prior fiscal year period as the instrument was fully settled upon maturity, and recognized a change in fair value of its warrants, resulting in a gain of&#160;$2.2&#160;million compared to a loss of&#160;$1.4 million as a result of the change in our share price and the exercise price of the instrument. The Company recognized a gain of $9.6&#160;million resulting from the changes in foreign exchange rates during the period&#160;compared to a loss&#160;of&#160;$4.1&#160;million&#160;for the prior fiscal year period. The Company recognized a loss on long-term investments, resulting in a loss of&#160;$5.6&#160;million&#160;as a result of a change in fair value of certain long-term investments&#160;compared to&#160;loss of&#160;$0.2 million for the prior&#160;period. The other non-operating (losses) gains, net were&#160;$4.0 million&#160;for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, which was&#160;mainly&#160;comprised of&#160;a gain&#160;of $5.8 million&#160;resulting from the exchange transaction of&#160;the TLRY 27 Notes, see Note 17&#160;(Convertible debentures payable). The other non-operating (losses) gains, net for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2024 were&#160;$12.4&#160;million and were mainly&#160;comprised&#160;of&#160;$2.3 million relating to the&#160;downside protection on the share issuance relating to the HTI note, $2.5&#160;million&#160; to settle outstanding&#160;notes with non-controlling interest shareholders, $4.6 million related to the&#160;decrease in value of equity investee, Cannfections, and $3.1 million of&#160;loss on measurement&#160;at the lower of carrying amount and the fair value less costs to sell of Broken Coast&#8217;s former Duncan facility.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures to GAAP Measures</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Adjusted EBITDA</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure that does not have a standardized meaning prescribed by GAAP and may not be comparable to similar measures presented by other companies. The Company calculates adjusted EBITDA as net loss/net income before income taxes, net interest expense, depreciation and amortization, equity in net loss of equity-method investees, purchase price accounting step-up on inventory,&#160;stock-based compensation, inventory valuation adjustments, impairments, other than temporary change in fair value of convertible notes receivable, Project 420 business optimization, loss (gain) on sale of capital assets - non-operating facility, restructuring costs, transaction (income) costs, net,&#160;litigation costs net of recoveries, change in fair value of contingent consideration,&#160;unrealized currency gains and losses and other adjustments.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">We believe&#160;that this presentation provides useful information to management, analysts and investors regarding certain additional financial and business trends relating to our results of operations and financial condition. In addition, management uses this measure for reviewing the financial results of the Company and as a component of performance-based executive compensation decisions.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">We do not consider adjusted EBITDA in isolation or as an alternative to financial measures determined in accordance with GAAP. The principal limitation of adjusted EBITDA is that it excludes certain expenses and income that are required by U.S. GAAP to be recorded in our consolidated financial statements. In addition, adjusted EBITDA is subject to inherent limitations as this metric reflects the exercise of judgment by management about which expenses and income are excluded or included in determining adjusted EBITDA. In order to compensate for these limitations, management presents adjusted EBITDA in connection with GAAP results.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">For the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, adjusted EBITDA decreased by $5.4 million to $55.0 million compared to&#160;$60.5 in the prior fiscal year&#160;as we continue to integrate our recent craft beverage acquisitions.</p>
