   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c131140931" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Fair value measurements</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. The carrying values of accounts receivable, prepaids and other current assets, bank indebtedness and accounts payable and accrued liabilities approximate their fair values due to their short periods to maturity. The Company calculates the estimated fair value of financial instruments, including convertible notes receivable, long-term investments, warrant liability, contingent consideration, and convertible debentures, using quoted market prices when available. When quoted market prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, fair value is determined based on valuation techniques using the best information available and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include quoted market prices, market comparable, and discounted cash flow projections.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c131140932" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Income taxes</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Income taxes are recognized in the consolidated statements of loss and comprehensive loss and are comprised of current and deferred taxes. Current tax is recognized in connection with income for tax purposes, unrealized tax benefits and the recovery of tax paid in a prior period and measured using enacted tax rates and laws applicable to the taxation period during which the income for tax purposes arose. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are determined based on the differences between the financial reporting and the tax basis of assets and liabilities and are measured using the enacted tax rates and laws that will be in effect when the differences are expected to reverse. Management makes an assessment of the likelihood that a deferred tax asset will be realized, and a valuation allowance is provided to the extent that it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that all or a portion of a deferred tax asset will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be realized.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The Company recognizes uncertain income tax positions at the largest amount that is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to be sustained upon audit by the relevant tax authority. An uncertain income tax position will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be recognized if it has less than a <em style="font: inherit;">50%</em> likelihood of being sustained. A change in the recognition or measurement of an unrealized tax benefit is reflected in the period during which the change occurs.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerPolicyTextBlock" id="c131140933" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Revenue</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Revenue is recognized when the control of the promised goods or services, through performance obligation, is transferred or provided to the customer in an amount that reflects the consideration we expect to be entitled to in exchange for the performance obligations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Excise taxes&#160;remitted&#160;to tax authorities are government-imposed excise taxes on cannabis and beer. Excise taxes are recorded as a reduction of sales in net revenue in the consolidated statements of loss and comprehensive loss&#160;and recognized as a current liability within accounts payable and accrued liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets, with the liability subsequently reduced when the taxes are remitted to the tax authority.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In addition, amounts disclosed as net revenue are net of excise taxes, sales tax, duty tax, allowances, discounts and rebates.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In determining the transaction price for the sale of goods or services, the Company considers the effects of variable consideration and the existence of significant financing components, if any.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">We&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>enter into certain contracts for the sale of goods or services, which provide customers with rights of return, volume discounts, bonuses for volume/quality achievement, and/or sales allowances. In addition, the Company&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>provide in certain circumstances, a retrospective price reduction to a customer based primarily on inventory movement. The inclusion of these items&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>give rise to variable consideration. The Company uses the expected value method to estimate the variable consideration because&#160;this method provides the most accurate estimation of the amount of variable consideration to which the Company will be entitled. The Company uses historical evidence, current information and forecasts to estimate the variable consideration. The Company reduces revenue and recognizes a contract liability, recorded in accounts receivable, net, equal to the amount expected to be refunded to the customer in the form of a future rebate or credit for a retrospective price reduction, representing its obligation to return the customer&#8217;s consideration. The estimate is updated at each reporting period date.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"></p>

   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31" name="us-gaap:CostOfSalesPolicyTextBlock" id="c131140934" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Cost of goods sold </i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Cost of goods sold represents costs directly related to manufacturing and distribution of the Company&#8217;s products. Primary costs include raw materials, packaging, direct labor, overhead, shipping and handling, the amortization of manufacturing equipment and production facilities and tariffs. Manufacturing overhead and related expenses include salaries, wages, employee benefits, utilities, maintenance and property taxes. Cost of goods sold also includes inventory valuation adjustments.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31" name="tlry:GeneralAndAdministrativeExpensesPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c131140935" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i>General and administrative </i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">General and administrative expenses are comprised primarily of (i) personnel related costs such as salaries, benefits, annual employee bonus expense and stock-based compensation costs; (ii) legal, accounting, consulting and other professional fees; and (iii) corporate insurance and other facilities costs associated with our corporate and administrative locations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31" name="tlry:SellingPolicyTextBlock" id="c131140936" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Selling </i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Selling expenses are comprised of direct selling costs which primarily consist of (i) commissions paid to our <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party workforce, (ii) patient acquisition and maintenance fees, (iii) Health Canada&#8217;s cannabis fees and (iv) outbound freight.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31" name="tlry:MarketingAndPromotionsPolicyTextBlock" id="c131140937" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Marketing and promotion</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Marketing and promotion expenses are comprised primarily of marketing and advertising expenses.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31" name="us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpensePolicy" id="c131140938" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Research and development</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Research and development costs are expensed as incurred. Research and development are comprised primarily of costs for&#160;clinical study costs, contracted research, consulting services, materials, supplies&#160;and other expenses incurred to sustain our overall research and development programs.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" id="c131140939" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Stock-based compensation</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The Company has an omnibus plan which includes issuances of stock options, restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;) and stock appreciation rights (&#8220;SARs&#8221;). The Company estimates the fair value of stock options on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes option pricing model. The fair value of RSUs is based on the share price as at date of grant and <ix:nonFraction id="c131139876" contextRef="i_2025-05-31_AwardTypeAxis-StockAppreciationRightsSARSMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsNonvestedNumber" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> SARs were issued to date. The share-based compensation expense is based on the fair value of the stock-based awards at the grant date and the expense is recognized over the related service period following a straight-line vesting expense schedule. The Company estimates forfeitures at the time of grant and revises these estimates in subsequent periods if actual forfeitures differ from those estimates. Any revisions are recognized in the consolidated statements of loss and comprehensive loss such that the cumulative expense reflects the revised estimate.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">For performance-based stock options and RSUs, the Company records compensation expense over the estimated service period adjusted for a probability factor of achieving the performance-based milestones. At each reporting date, the Company assesses the probability factor and records compensation expense accordingly, net of estimated forfeitures.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31" name="tlry:TransactionCostsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c131140940" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Transaction (income) costs, net</i>&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The Company expenses costs net of any gains directly attributable to business acquisitions and classifies these items as transaction (income) costs, net. These items&#160;include among other things, legal fees to complete the acquisition, financial advisor and due diligence costs, and transaction related compensation. These items are recognized&#160;as incurred.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" id="c131140941" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Earnings (loss) per share</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Basic earnings (loss) per share is computed by dividing reported net income (loss) attributable to stockholders of Tilray Brands, Inc. by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the year. Diluted earnings (loss) per share is computed by dividing reported net income (loss) attributable to stockholders of Tilray Brands, Inc. by the sum of the weighted average number of common shares and the number of dilutive potential common share equivalents outstanding during the period. Potential dilutive common share equivalents consist of the incremental common shares issuable upon the exercise of vested share options, warrants, and RSUs and the incremental shares issuable upon conversion of the convertible debentures and similar instruments. Shares of common stock outstanding under the&#160;share lending&#160;arrangement entered into in conjunction with the TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes, see Note&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">17</em>&#160;(Convertible debentures payable) are excluded from the calculation of basic and diluted earnings per share&#160;because the borrower of the shares is required&#160;to refund any dividends paid on the shares lent under the share lending arrangement.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In computing diluted earnings (loss) per share, common share equivalents are&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;considered in periods in which a net loss is reported, as the inclusion of the common share equivalents would be anti-dilutive. For the fiscal years ended&#160;&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>&#160;and&#160;&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2024, </em>the dilutive potential common share equivalents outstanding consisted of the following: <ix:nonFraction id="c131139881" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember" unitRef="Share"    <p style="text-indent: 9pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="text-indent: 9pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="c131140942" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Critical accounting estimates and judgments</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The preparation of the Company&#8217;s financial statements requires management to make judgments, estimates and assumptions that affect the application of policies and reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses. These estimates and judgements are subject to change based on experience and new information which could result in outcomes that require a material adjustment to the carrying amounts of assets or liabilities affecting future periods. Actual results <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>differ from these estimates. The estimates and underlying assumptions are reviewed on an ongoing basis. Revisions to accounting estimates are recognized prospectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Financial statement areas that require significant judgement and estimates are as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <ix:exclude>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Estimated useful lives, impairment considerations and amortization of capital and intangible assets </i>&#8211;<i> </i>Amortization of capital and intangible assets is dependent upon estimates of useful lives based on management&#8217;s judgment.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible asset impairment testing require management to make estimates in the impairment testing model. On at least an annual basis, the Company tests whether goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets are impaired. Impairment of definite long-lived assets is influenced by judgment in defining a reporting unit and determining the indicators of impairment, and estimates used to measure impairment losses.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The reporting unit&#8217;s fair value is determined using discounted future cash flow models, which incorporate assumptions regarding future events, specifically future cash flows, growth rates, probability of anticipated EU and U.S. cannabis regulatory changes&#160;and discount rates.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Business combinations </i>&#8211;<i> </i>Judgement is used in determining a) whether an acquisition is a business combination or an asset acquisition. We use judgement in applying the acquisition method of accounting for business combinations and estimates to value identifiable assets and liabilities at the acquisition date. Estimates are used to determine cash flow projections, including the period of future benefit, and future growth and discount rates, among other factors. The values allocated to the acquired assets and liabilities assumed affect the amount of goodwill recorded on acquisition. Fair value of assets acquired and liabilities assumed is typically estimated using an income approach, which is based on the present value of future discounted cash flows. Significant estimates in the discounted cash flow model include the discount rate, rate of future revenue growth and profitability of the acquired business and working capital effects. The discount rate considers the relevant risk associated with the business-specific characteristics and the uncertainty related to the ability to achieve projected cash flows. These estimates and the resulting valuations require significant judgment. Management engages <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party experts to assist in the valuation of material acquisitions.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Convertible debentures </i>&#8211;<i> </i>The fair value of Convertible Debentures where the Company had elected the fair value option are determined using the Black-Scholes option pricing model. Assumptions and estimates are made in determining an appropriate conversion price, volatility, dividend yield, and the fair value of common stock. There is judgement in assessing what portion of the gain or loss, if any, relates to the change in the instrument-specific credit risk.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c131140943" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i>New accounting pronouncements <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> yet adopted</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> August 2023,&#160;</em>the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;)&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05,</em>&#160;Business Combination - Joint Venture Formations&#160;(Subtopic&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">805</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">60</em>) Recognition and Initial Measurement (&#8220;ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05&#8221;</em>), which is intended to address the accounting for contributions made to a joint venture. ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05</em>&#160;is effective for the Company beginning&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2026.&#160;</em>This update will be applied prospectively and the Company is currently evaluating the effect of adopting this ASU.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> October&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em>&#160;the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">06,</em>&#160;Disclosure Improvements: Codification Amendments in Response to the SEC&#8217;s Disclosure Update and Simplification Initiative,&#160;which amends the disclosure or presentation requirements related to various subtopics in the FASB Accounting Standards Codification (the &#8220;Codification&#8221;). The effective date for each amendment will be the date on which the SEC&#8217;s removal of that related disclosure from Regulation S-<em style="font: inherit;">X</em>&#160;or Regulation S-K becomes effective, with early adoption prohibited. If by&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2027,&#160;</em>the SEC has&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;removed the applicable requirement from Regulation S-<em style="font: inherit;">X</em>&#160;or Regulation S-K, the pending content of the related amendment will be removed from the Codification and will&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;become effective for any entity.&#160;The Company is currently evaluating the effect of adopting this ASU.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In&#160;&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023,&#160;</em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em>&#160;Income Taxes (Topic&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">740</em>)&#160;Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures,&#160;which requires public entities to disclose specific categories in the rate reconciliation and provide additional information for reconciling items that meet a quantitative threshold on an annual basis. ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em>&#160;is effective for the Company&#160;beginning&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2025.&#160;</em>The Company is currently evaluating the effect of adopting this ASU.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024,&#160;</em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em>&#160;Income Statement&#8212;Reporting Comprehensive Income&#8212;Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses,&#160;which requires disaggregated disclosure of income statement expenses for public business entities. ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em>&#160;is effective for the Company beginning&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2026.&#160;</em>The Company is currently evaluating the effect of adopting this ASU.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024,&#160;</em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">04,</em>&#160;Debt with Conversion and Other Options (Subtopic&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">470</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">20</em>): Induced Conversions of Convertible Debt Instruments,&#160;which seeks to clarify the requirements for determining whether certain settlements of convertible debt instruments should be accounted for as an induced conversion. ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">04</em>&#160;is effective for the Company beginning&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2025.&#160;</em>The Company is currently evaluating the effect of adopting this ASU.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>New accounting pronouncements recently adopted</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em>&#160;the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">07,</em>&#160;Segment Reporting (Topic&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">280</em>) Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures,&#160;which requires public entities to disclose information about their reportable segments&#8217; significant expenses on an interim and annual basis.&#160;Refer to Note <em style="font: inherit;">30</em>&#160;for the incremental disclosures required under ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">07.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;"></p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">During the fiscal year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2024,&#160;</em>the Company classified $<ix:nonFraction id="c131139946" contextRef="i_2024-05-31_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-DuncanQuebecAndFortCollinsFacilitiesMember_RealEstatePropertiesAxis-BrokenCoastCannabisLtdMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AssetsHeldForSaleNotPartOfDisposalGroup" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">32,074</ix:nonFraction>&#160;of the following assets from its Cannabis reporting segment as assets held for sale, including its&#160;Quebec cultivation facility, the Fort Collins, CO partially vacant warehouse facility, and the Broken Coast&#160;former cultivation facility located in Duncan, B.C. Following an&#160;assessment of facility capacity utilization, it was determined that these facilities would be exited and held for sale.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">During the fiscal year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025, </em>the Company sold the former Broken Coast&#160;cultivation facility.&#160;Additionally,&#160;due to a change in circumstance in the Company's intention to sell our Quebec cultivation facility, the asset was subsequently reclassified as capital assets as the Company has made alternative plans for its utilization. The asset&#160;was&#160;then remeasured at the lower of its carrying amount before being classified as held for sale less the amortization that would have occurred and the fair value on the date the decision&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;to proceed with a sale was made. Changes in the carrying amount were&#160;recorded in the consolidated statement of net loss and comprehensive loss&#160;as amortization in cost of goods sold.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">During the preceding quarter ended <em style="font: changes in U.S. global economic policy, including slower than anticipated progress in global cannabis legalization and overall declines in the craft beer industry sector,&#160;the Company concluded that it is more likely than&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not,</em>&#160;that the fair value of our reporting units were&#160;less than their carrying amounts as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2025. </em>Accordingly, the Company utilized the income approach, which uses future discounted cash flows, to determine the fair value of each reporting unit.&#160;As a result, the    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>MedMen Convertible Note</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> August 31, 2021,&#160;</em>the Company issued&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c131140074" contextRef="d_2021-08-31_2021-08-31_AssetAcquisitionAxis-TheMMNotesAndMMWarrantsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesAcquisitions" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">9,817,061</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares valued at $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140075" contextRef="d_2021-08-31_2021-08-31_AssetAcquisitionAxis-TheMMNotesAndMMWarrantsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodValueAcquisitions" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">117,804</ix:nonFraction>&#160;to acquire&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c131140076" contextRef="i_2021-08-31_OwnershipAxis-SuperheroAcquisitionLPMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:MinorityInterestOwnershipPercentageByParent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">68</ix:nonFraction>% interest in Superhero Acquisition L.P. (&#8220;SH Acquisition&#8221;), which purchased a senior secured convertible note issued by MedMen (the "MedMen Convertible Note"), together with certain associated warrants to acquire Class B subordinate voting shares of MedMen, in the principal amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140077" contextRef="i_2021-08-31_AccountsNotesLoansAndFinancingReceivableByReceivableTypeAxis-MMNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:NotesReceivableNet" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">165,799</ix:nonFraction>. The MedMen Convertible Note bears interest at the Secured Overnight Financing Rate ("SOFR") plus&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c131140078" contextRef="d_2021-08-31_2021-08-31_AccountsNotesLoansAndFinancingReceivableByReceivableTypeAxis-MMNotesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="tlry:NotesReceivableInterestRateBasisSpreadOnVariableRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">6</ix:nonFraction>%, with a SOFR floor of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c131140079" contextRef="i_2021-08-31_AccountsNotesLoansAndFinancingReceivableByReceivableTypeAxis-MMNotesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="tlry:NotesReceivableSOFRFloor" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">2.5</ix:nonFraction>% with any accrued interest being added to the outstanding principal amount. The outstanding principal amount, together with accrued interest&#160;is to be paid on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> August 17, 2028,&#160;</em>the&#160;maturity date of the MedMen Convertible Note. SH Acquisition was also granted &#8220;top-up&#8221; rights enabling it (and its limited partners) to maintain its percentage ownership (on an &#8220;as-converted&#8221; basis) in the event that MedMen issues equity securities.&#160;SH Acquisition&#8217;s ability to convert the MedMen Convertible Note&#160;and exercise the Warrants is dependent upon U.S. federal legalization of cannabis or Tilray&#8217;s waiver of such requirement as well as any additional regulatory approvals.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">During the fiscal year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>,&#160;the Company recognized an&#160;other-than-temporary change in fair value, which resulted in a non-cash expense&#160;of $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140080" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31_AccountsNotesLoansAndFinancingReceivableByReceivableTypeAxis-MMNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncreaseDecreaseInNotesReceivables" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7" sign="-">20,000</ix:nonFraction> compared to $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140081" contextRef="d_2023-06-01_2024-05-31_AccountsNotesLoansAndFinancingReceivableByReceivableTypeAxis-MMNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncreaseDecreaseInNotesReceivables" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3" sign="-">42,681</ix:nonFraction>&#160;for the fiscal year&#160;ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31,&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2024.</em> The&#160;MedMen Convertible Note was valued based upon the fair value of the&#160;collateral assets net of disposal costs and has been reduced to reflect recent developments in restructuring efforts.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As&#160;&#160;previously disclosed, MedMen and certain of its subsidiaries commenced insolvency actions in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> April 2024.&#160;&#160;</em>On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 16, 2025,&#160;</em>MedMen exited receivership and substantially all of its remaining assets were transferred to a new entity owned by MedMen&#8217;s secured creditors, including SH Acquisition. In connection with the foregoing, the Company disposed&#160;of its MedMen Convertible Note in exchange for an option to acquire a&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c131140083" contextRef="i_2025-01-16_OwnershipAxis-SuperheroAcquisitionLPMember_StatementScenarioAxis-UponUsFederalCannabisLegalizationMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:MinorityInterestOwnershipPercentageByParent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">68</ix:nonFraction>% membership interest in&#160;SH Acquisition&#160;for $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140084" contextRef="i_2025-01-16_OwnershipAxis-SuperheroAcquisitionLPMember_StatementScenarioAxis-UponUsFederalCannabisLegalizationMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="tlry:EquityInvestmentStrikePrice" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1.00</ix:nonFraction>&#160;upon U.S. federal cannabis legalization.&#160;See Note <em style="font: inherit;">12</em>&#160;(Long-term investments). As a result, the Company&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;longer controls SH Acquisition and thus&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;longer consolidates this entity for accounting purposes and as a result&#160;the Company recognized $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140088" contextRef="d_2025-01-16_2025-01-16_AccountsNotesLoansAndFinancingReceivableByReceivableTypeAxis-MMNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncreaseDecreaseInNotesReceivables" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,661</ix:nonFraction> of other-than-temporary change in fair value as part of this disposal.&#160;See Note&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">21</em> (Non-controlling interests).</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">The Company&#160;did&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;derive any revenue or cash from MedMen's operations, and fully complies with all limitations imposed by applicable U.S. law and regulations in connection with its ownership of the MedMen Convertible Note and/or its option to acquire SH Acquisition.&#160;In addition, since the fiscal year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2024,&#160;</em>the Company has&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140091">not</span>&#160;recognized any&#160;interest income on the MedMen Convertible Note,&#160;nor&#160;did the Company recognize any interest income for the fiscal year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>, which would have&#160;increased&#160;its value.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) was enacted on <em style="font: inherit;"> December 22, 2017 </em>and reduced the U.S. statutory federal corporate tax rate from <ix:nonFraction id="c131140109" contextRef="d_2017-12-22_2017-12-22" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">35</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction id="c131140110" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">21</ix:nonFraction>% and introduced several new international tax provisions, including the tax on Global Intangible Low-Taxed Income (&#8216;&#8216;GILTI&#8217;&#8217;). The Company has made a policy decision to record GILTI tax as a current-period expense when incurred.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> July 4, 2025, </em>the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (&#8220;OBBBA&#8221;) was enacted, which extended and modified certain provisions of the TCJA, including bonus depreciation and interest expense limitations. As the enactment occurred after the Company&#8217;s fiscal year-end, the impact of the OBBBA is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reflected in these Financial Statements. The Company is evaluating the potential impact of the new legislation on future periods but does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect a material impact to the Financial Statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Deferred income taxes have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been recorded on the basis differences for investments in consolidated subsidiaries as these basis differences are indefinitely reinvested or will reverse in a non-taxable manner. Quantification of the deferred income tax liability, if any, associated with indefinitely reinvested basis differences is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> practicable. Deferred income taxes have been recorded on the basis differences for investments in nonconsolidated entities.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>, the Company had generated net operating loss carry-forwards in the United States of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140115" contextRef="i_2025-05-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">314,512</ix:nonFraction>, which can be carried forward indefinitely and are generally limited in use annually to <ix:nonFraction id="c131140116" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember" unitRef="Pure" name="tlry:NetOperatingLossCarryforwardsOffsetPercentageOfTaxableIncome" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">80</ix:nonFraction>% of the current year taxable income, starting <em style="font: inherit;">2021.</em> The Company has generated&#160;net operating loss carry-forwards in Canada of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140118" contextRef="i_2025-05-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-ForeignCountryMember_IncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis-CanadaRevenueAgencyMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,544,987</ix:nonFraction>, which&#160;can be carried forward for <em style="font: inherit;">20</em> years and begin to expire in <em style="font: inherit;">2028.</em> Management believes that it is more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that the benefit from certain United States and foreign net operating loss carry-forwards will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be realized. In recognition of this risk, the Company has provided a valuation allowance on the deferred tax assets relating to these carry-forwards. The net change in the total valuation allowance was an increase of $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140123" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31_ValuationAllowancesAndReservesTypeAxis-ValuationAllowanceOfDeferredTaxAssetsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowancesAndReservesPeriodIncreaseDecrease" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">179,090</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140124" contextRef="d_2023-06-01_2024-05-31_ValuationAllowancesAndReservesTypeAxis-ValuationAllowanceOfDeferredTaxAssetsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowancesAndReservesPeriodIncreaseDecrease" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">164,471</ix:nonFraction> for the fiscal years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively. The net change in the total valuation allowance was primarily a result of current year losses.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The Company recognizes the financial statement impact of a tax position only after determining that the relevant tax authority would more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> sustain the position following an audit. For tax positions meeting the more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> threshold, the amount recognized in the Financial Statements is the largest impact that has a greater than <em style="font: inherit;">fifty</em> percent likelihood of being realized upon ultimate settlement with the relevant tax authority.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The total amount of gross unrecognized tax benefits (&#8220;GUTB&#8221;) was <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140129">$nil,</span> <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140130">$nil,</span> and <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140131">$nil</span>&#160;as of <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> respectively. There is a reasonable possibility that the Company&#8217;s unrecognized tax benefits will change within <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months due to audit settlements or the expiration of statute of limitations, but the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect the change to be material to&#160;Financial Statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The Company recognizes interest and, if applicable, penalties for any uncertain tax positions. Interest and penalties are recorded as a component of income tax expenses. In the fiscal years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, the Company recorded approximately <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140138">$nil,</span> <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140139">$nil</span>&#160;and <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140140">$nil,</span> respectively, of interest and penalty expenses related to uncertain tax positions. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>, and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, the Company had a cumulative balance of accrued interest and penalties on unrecognized tax positions of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140142">$nil</span> and <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140143">$nil,</span> respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The Company and its subsidiaries are subject to United States federal income tax as well as the income tax of multiple state and foreign jurisdictions. Major jurisdictions where there are wholly owned subsidiaries of Tilray Brands, Inc. which require income tax filings include Canada, Portugal, Germany, and Australia. The earliest periods open for review by local taxing authorities are fiscal years <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140144">2021</span>&#160;for Canada, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140145">2021</span>&#160;for Portugal, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140146">2020</span>&#160;for Germany, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140147">2021</span>&#160;for Australia, and <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140148">2022</span>&#160;for United States.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;convertible debentures&#160;were issued&#160;on&#160;&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 30, 2023&#160;</em>and on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 9, 2023, </em>by way of overallotment,&#160;in the principal amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140203" contextRef="i_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">172,500</ix:nonFraction>&#160;(the &#8220;TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes&#8221;). The TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes&#160;bear interest at a rate of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c131140206" contextRef="i_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">5.20</ix:nonFraction>% per annum, payable semi-annually in arrears on&#160;&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 15&#160;</em>and&#160;&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 15&#160;</em>of each year, and mature on&#160;&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 15, 2027,&#160;</em>unless earlier converted. The TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes are Tilray&#8217;s general unsecured obligations and rank senior in right of payment to all of Tilray&#8217;s indebtedness that is expressly subordinated in right of payment to the notes; equal in right of payment with any of Tilray&#8217;s unsecured indebtedness that is&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;so subordinated,&#160;effectively junior in right of payment to any of Tilray&#8217;s secured indebtedness to the extent of the value of the assets securing such indebtedness; and structurally junior to all indebtedness and other liabilities (including trade payables but excluding intercompany obligations) of Tilray&#8217;s current or future subsidiaries.&#160;Noteholders have the right to convert their TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes into shares of Tilray&#8217;s Common Stock at their option, at any time, until the close of business on the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">second</em>&#160;scheduled trading day immediately before&#160;&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 15, 2027.&#160;</em>The initial conversion rate is&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c131140211" contextRef="d_2023-05-30_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleConversionRatio1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">376.6478</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares per&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c131140212" contextRef="i_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="USD" name="tlry:DebtInstrumentConvertibleMultiplesOfPrincipalAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;principal amount of TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes, which represents a conversion price of approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c131140214" contextRef="i_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleConversionPrice1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2.66</ix:nonFraction>&#160;per share. The conversion rate and conversion price will be subject to adjustment upon the occurrence of certain events.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes will be redeemable, in whole and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;in part, at Tilray&#8217;s option at any time on or after <em style="font: inherit;"> June 20, 2025&#160;</em>at a cash redemption price equal to the principal amount of the notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, to, but excluding, the redemption date, but only if the last reported sale price of Tilray&#8217;s Common Stock exceeds&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c131140217" contextRef="d_2023-05-30_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleThresholdPercentageOfStockPriceTrigger" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">130</ix:nonFraction>% of the conversion price for a specified period of time. If certain corporate events that constitute a fundamental change occur, then, subject to a limited exception, noteholders&#160;&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>require&#160;Tilray&#160;to repurchase their TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes for cash. The repurchase price will be equal to the principal amount of the notes to be repurchased, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, to, but excluding, the applicable repurchase date. In connection with the Company&#8217;s offering of the TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes, the Company entered into a share lending agreement with an affiliate of&#160;Jefferies LLC&#160;(the &#8220;Share Borrower&#8221;), pursuant to which it lent&#160;to the Share Borrower&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c131140220" contextRef="i_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:OwnshareLendingArrangementSharesIssued" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">38,500,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of the Company&#8217;s Common Stock (the &#8220;Borrowed Shares&#8221;). The Borrowed Shares were newly-issued shares,&#160;will be held as treasury shares until the expiration or early termination of the share lending agreement&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>be used by purchasers of the TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes&#160;to sell up to&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c131140222" contextRef="i_2023-05-30_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:OwnshareLendingArrangementSharesIssued" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">38,500,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of the Company&#8217;s Common Stock. The fair value of the share lending agreement has been recorded as part of the unamortized discount on the debenture. The Company expects that the selling stockholders will use their position created by such sales to establish their initial hedge with respect to their investments in the TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes. The Company did&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;receive any proceeds from the sale of the Borrowed Shares.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">During the fiscal year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>,&#160;the Company exchanged an aggregate $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140225" contextRef="i_2025-05-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentRepurchaseAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">67,500</ix:nonFraction> of its TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes for cancellation, by issuing&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c131140227" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="Share" name="tlry:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesForTheRepaymentOfConvertibleDebt" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">71,755,054</ix:nonFraction> shares of Common Stock and paying $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140228" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RepaymentsOfConvertibleDebt" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">9,335</ix:nonFraction> in cash to settle accrued interest. Upon exchanging&#160;the TLRY&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">27</em>&#160;Notes, a portion of the&#160;settlement consideration was allocated to the equity component of the instrument and&#160;was&#160;recognized as a $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140230" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-TLRY27Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AdjustmentsToAdditionalPaidInCapitalConvertibleDebtWithConversionFeature" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">19,028</ix:nonFraction> reduction of additional paid-in capital in the Consolidated Statements of Stockholders&#8217; Equity.    <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2024, </em>there were <ix:nonFraction id="c131140254" contextRef="i_2025-05-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightOutstanding" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">6,209,000</ix:nonFraction> warrants outstanding, with an original exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140255" contextRef="i_2025-05-31" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">5.95</ix:nonFraction> per warrant, expiring <em style="font: inherit;"> September 17, 2025. </em>Each warrant is exercisable for <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140256"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140820">one</span></span> common share of the Company.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The warrants contain anti-dilution price protection features, which adjust the exercise price of the warrants if the Company subsequently issues common stock at a price lower than the exercise price of the warrants. In the event additional warrants or convertible debt are issued with a lower and/or variable exercise price, the exercise price of the warrants will be adjusted accordingly. During the fiscal year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>, the Company issued shares which triggered the anti-dilution price protection feature lowering the exercise price to $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140257" contextRef="i_2025-05-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.42</ix:nonFraction>. These warrants are classified as liabilities as they are to be settled in registered shares, and the registration statement is required to be active, unless such shares <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be subject to an applicable exemption from registration requirements. The holders, at their sole discretion, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>elect to affect a cashless exercise, and be issued exempt securities in accordance with Section <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>(a)(<em style="font: inherit;">9</em>) of the <em style="font: inherit;">1933</em> Act. In the event the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> maintain an effective registration statement, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be required to pay a daily cash penalty equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c131140262" contextRef="i_2025-05-31" unitRef="Pure" name="tlry:PercentageOfDailyCashPenalty" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">1</ix:nonFraction>% of the number of shares of common stock due to be issued multiplied by any trading price of the common stock between the exercise date and the share delivery date, as selected by the holder. Alternatively, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>deliver registered common stock purchased by the Company in the open market. The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also be required to pay cash if it does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have sufficient authorized shares to deliver to the holders upon exercise.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Tilray <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em> Equity Incentive Plan and Original Plan</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em> Equity Incentive Plan (EIP) authorizes the award of stock options, restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;) and stock appreciation rights (&#8220;SARs&#8221;) to employees, including officers, non-employee directors and consultants and the employees and consultants of our affiliates. Shares subject to awards granted under the EIP that expire or terminate without being exercised in full, or that are paid out in cash rather than in shares, do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reduce the number of shares available for issuance under the EIP. Additionally, shares become available for future grant under the EIP if they were issued under the EIP and if the Company repurchases them or they are forfeited. This includes shares used to pay the exercise price of an award or to satisfy the tax withholding obligations related to an award. The maximum number of shares of common stock subject to stock awards granted under the EIP or otherwise during any <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> calendar year to any non-employee director, taken together with any cash fees paid by the Company to such non-employee director during such calendar year for service on the Board of Directors, will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exceed <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140313">five hundred thousand</span> dollars in total value, calculating the value of any such stock awards based on the grant date fair value of such stock awards for financial reporting purposes, or, with respect to the calendar year in which a nonemployee director is <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> appointed or elected to our Board of Directors, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140315">one million</span> dollars.</p>
