   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Stock options represent the right to purchase shares of our common stock on the date of exercise at a stated exercise price. The exercise price of a stock option generally must be at least equal to the fair market value of our shares of common stock on the date of grant. The Company&#8217;s compensation committee <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>provide for stock options to be exercised only as they vest or to be immediately exercisable with any shares issued on exercise being subject to the Company&#8217;s right of repurchase that lapses as the shares vest. The maximum term of stock options granted under the EIP is <em style="font: inherit;">ten</em> years.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">RSUs represent a right to receive common stock or their cash equivalent for each RSU that vests, which vesting <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be based on time or achievement of performance conditions. Unless otherwise determined by our compensation committee at the time of grant, vesting will cease on the date the participant <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer provides services to the Company and unvested shares will be forfeited. If an RSU has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been forfeited, then on the date specified in the RSUs, the Company will deliver to the holder a number of whole shares of common stock, cash or a combination of shares of our common stock and cash. Additionally, dividend equivalents <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be credited in respect of shares covered by the RSUs. Any additional shares covered by the RSU credited by reason of such dividend equivalents will be subject to all of the same terms and conditions of the underlying RSU agreement to which they relate. The RSUs generally vest over a <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-TilrayTwoThousandAndEighteenEquityIncentivePlanAndOriginalPlanMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" id="c131140320" format="ixt-sec:duryear">3</ix:nonNumeric>-or-<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-TilrayTwoThousandAndEighteenEquityIncentivePlanAndOriginalPlanMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" id="c131140321" format="ixt-sec:duryear">4</ix:nonNumeric> year period. The fair value of RSUs are based on the share price as at date of grant.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">SARs provide for a payment, or payments, in cash or shares of common stock to the holder based upon the difference between the fair market value of shares of our common stock on the date of exercise and the stated exercise price. The maximum term of SARs granted under the EIP is <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140322">ten</span> years. <ix:nonFraction id="c131140323" contextRef="i_2025-05-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-TilrayTwoThousandAndEighteenEquityIncentivePlanAndOriginalPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsNonvestedNumber" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">No</ix:nonFraction> SARs were issued to date.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The EIP permits the grant of performance-based stock and cash awards. The performance goals <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be based on Company-wide performance or performance of <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more business units, divisions, affiliates or business segments and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be either absolute or relative to the performance of <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more comparable companies or the performance of <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more relevant indices. The length of any performance period, the performance goals to be achieved during the performance period, and the measure of whether and to what degree such performance goals have been attained will be conclusively determined by the Board of Directors.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">In conjunction with the reverse acquisition&#160;with Aphria Inc on <em style="font: inherit;"> April 30, 2021, </em><ix:nonFraction id="c131140327" contextRef="i_2025-05-31_PlanNameAxis-TilrayTwoThousandAndEighteenEquityIncentivePlanAndOriginalPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">9,806,851</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock had been reserved for issuance under the EIP. The number of shares of common stock reserved for issuance under the <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em> EIP will automatically increase on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1 </em>of each calendar year, for a period of <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> more than <em style="font: inherit;">ten</em> years, starting on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2019 </em>and ending on and including <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2027, </em>in an amount equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c131140331" contextRef="i_2025-05-31_PlanNameAxis-TilrayTwoThousandAndEighteenEquityIncentivePlanAndOriginalPlanMember" unitRef="Pure" name="tlry:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuanceAnnualAutomaticIncreasePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">4</ix:nonFraction>% of the total number of shares of our common stock outstanding on <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31 </em>of the prior calendar year, or a lesser number of shares determined by our Board of Directors. The shares reserved include only the outstanding shares related to stock options and RSUs and excludes stock options outstanding under the Original Plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Certain employees and other service providers of the Company participate in the equity-based compensation plan of Privateer Holdings, Inc (the &#8220;Original Plan&#8221;) under the terms and valuation method detailed below. The expected life of the stock options represented the period of time stock options were expected to be outstanding and was estimated considering vesting terms and employees&#8217; historical exercise and post-vesting employment termination behavior. Expected volatility was based on historical volatilities of public companies operating in a similar industry to Privateer Holdings. The risk-free rate is based on the United States Treasury yield curve in effect at the time of grant. The expected dividend yield was determined based on the stock option&#8217;s exercise price and expected annual dividend rate at the time of grant.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Predecessor Plan - Aphria</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Aphria had established the Aphria Omnibus Incentive Plan (the &#8220;Aphria Predecessor Plan&#8221;). Following stockholder approval of the EIP, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> new awards have been granted under the Aphria Predecessor Plan. In connection with the reverse acquisition Aphria stock options, Aphria RSUs and DSUs issued under the Predecessor Plan were exchanged for options, RSUs under the EIP. As a result of the modification, all grantees were affected, and the Company recognized <em style="font: inherit;">nil</em> incremental compensation cost.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 54pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Prior to the acquisition of HEXO Corp, HEXO had established the Formal Plan and Omnibus Incentive Plan (the &#8220;HEXO Predecessor Plan&#8221;). In connection with the acquisition, HEXO&#160;stock options issued under these plans were exchanged at a rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c131140342" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HexoMember_PlanNameAxis-PredecessorPlanMember" unitRef="Pure" name="tlry:BusinessCombinationCommonShareExchangeRatio" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.4352</ix:nonFraction> for <ix:nonFraction id="c131140343" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HexoMember_PlanNameAxis-PredecessorPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="tlry:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardOptionsConvertedUponAcquisitionNumber" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,267,793</ix:nonFraction> options under the Tilray <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em> EIP.    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Within the Cannabis segment, our restructuring costs predominantly related to&#160;the&#160;HEXO acquisition, which were&#160;completed within&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">24</em>&#160;months from the acquisition in <em style="font: inherit;"> June 2023.&#160;</em>In the fiscal year&#160;ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>,&#160;we&#160;recognized&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c131140383" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-TrussBeverageCompanyMember_RestructuringCostAndReserveAxis-EmployeeSeveranceMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCosts" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">10,404</ix:nonFraction> of expenses related to employee termination severance and benefits and other costs related to&#160;the conversion of the HEXO Quebec cultivation facility from cannabis to produce, the optimization of our Redecan facilities, and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c131140384" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-TrussBeverageCompanyMember_RestructuringCostAndReserveAxis-FacilityClosingMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCosts" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">987</ix:nonFraction> of restructuring charges related to the remaining costs of exiting the Truss Beverage Co. (&#8220;Truss&#8221;) facility following its sale to a&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>&#160;party in the fiscal year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2024.&#160;</em>Additionally, the Company recognized $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140386" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-AvantiFacilityMember_RestructuringCostAndReserveAxis-FacilityClosingMember_StatementBusinessSegmentsAxis-CannabisSegmentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCosts" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,133</ix:nonFraction> of costs associated with the winding down of our Avanti facility, which was exited and sold during the fiscal year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025.&#160;</em>The Company also recognized $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140387" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31_RestructuringCostAndReserveAxis-FacilityClosingMember_StatementBusinessSegmentsAxis-CannabisSegmentMember_StatementGeographicalAxis-CA-QC" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCosts" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,054</ix:nonFraction>&#160;of exit&#160;cost in connection with the termination of its contract with its distribution partner in the Quebec adult-use cannabis market and the insourcing of the&#160;function.    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Legal proceedings</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In the ordinary course of business, we are at times subject to various legal proceedings and disputes, including the proceedings specifically discussed below. We assess our liabilities and contingencies in connection with outstanding legal proceedings utilizing the latest information available. Where it is probable that we will incur a loss and the amount of the loss can be reasonably estimated, we record a liability in our consolidated financial statements. These legal reserves <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be increased or decreased to reflect any relevant developments on a quarterly basis. Where a loss is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> probable or the amount of loss is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> estimable, we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> accrue legal reserves. While the outcome of legal proceedings is inherently uncertain, based on information currently available and available insurance coverage, our management believes that it has established appropriate legal reserves. Any incremental liabilities arising from pending legal proceedings are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a material adverse effect on our consolidated financial position, consolidated results of operations, or consolidated cash flows. However, it is possible that the ultimate resolution of these matters, if unfavorable, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be material to our consolidated financial position, consolidated results of operations, or consolidated cash flows.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Class Action Suits and Stockholder Derivative Suits</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i>Settlement and Dismissal of Aphria Securities Class Action (Canada)</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 2019,&#160;</em>a putative securities class action was commenced in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice against Tilray&#8217;s wholly-owned subsidiary, Aphria, Inc. (&#8220;Aphria&#8221;), and certain of its former officers and directors (the &#8220;Aphria Canadian Class Action&#8221;). The Aphria Canadian Class Action was subsequently amended in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 2022&#160;</em>to proceed only against Aphria and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">two</em>&#160;of its former officers and directors as named defendants.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The class plaintiff sought damages in the amount of CAD $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140417" contextRef="d_2022-09-01_2022-09-30_LitigationCaseAxis-AphiraClassActionMember_LitigationStatusAxis-PendingLitigationMember_LossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis-DamagesMember" unitRef="CAD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyDamagesSoughtValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">875,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;pursuant to Ontario securities legislation on behalf of all class members who acquired Aphria&#8217;s common shares between&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 29, 2018&#160;</em>and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 3, 2018.&#160;</em>The Aphria Canadian Class Action stemmed from Aphria&#8217;s acquisition of Nuuvera Inc. and LATAM Holdings Inc. in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March&#160;</em>and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 2018,&#160;</em>respectively, alleging that the value of the acquired assets was misrepresented as being significantly higher than their actual worth, and that insiders at Aphria personally benefitted from the acquisitions at the expense of investors. Aphria and the individual defendants denied the allegations made in the Aphria Canadian Class Action and vigorously defended against them. Trial was scheduled to begin in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 5, 2025,&#160;</em>Aphria and the individual defendants successfully reached an agreement with the class plaintiff to settle the Aphria Canadian Class Action.&#160; The settlement agreement provided for the complete dismissal of the Aphria Canadian Class Action, with prejudice, in exchange for an aggregate payment from all defendants equal to CAD $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140418" contextRef="d_2025-02-05_2025-02-05_LitigationCaseAxis-AphiraClassActionMember_LitigationStatusAxis-SettledLitigationMember" unitRef="CAD" name="us-gaap:LitigationSettlementAmountAwardedToOtherParty" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">30,000</ix:nonFraction>, or approximately US $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140419" contextRef="d_2025-02-05_2025-02-05_LitigationCaseAxis-AphiraClassActionMember_LitigationStatusAxis-SettledLitigationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LitigationSettlementAmountAwardedToOtherParty" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">21,000</ix:nonFraction>,&#160;(the &#8220;Aphria Settlement Amount&#8221;).&#160;The settlement agreement also provided for the dismissal, with prejudice, of the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">four</em>&#160;individual Canadian lawsuits pursuing the same allegations of wrongdoing against Aphria and former and current officers and directors. The settlement does&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;constitute an admission of liability or wrongdoing by Aphria or the other defendants. The settlement agreement was approved by the Court on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 27, 2025 </em>and became effective on <em style="font: inherit;"> April 28, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The Aphria Settlement Amount was primarily funded by the outstanding balance under Aphria&#8217;s D&amp;O Insurance Policy and by the individual defendants. Aphria paid the remaining unpaid portion of the Settlement Amount equal to approximately CAD $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140422" contextRef="i_2025-02-28_LitigationCaseAxis-AphiraClassActionMember_LitigationStatusAxis-SettledLitigationMember" unitRef="CAD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualAtCarryingValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">8,300</ix:nonFraction>&#160;(or approximately US $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140423" contextRef="i_2025-02-28_LitigationCaseAxis-AphiraClassActionMember_LitigationStatusAxis-SettledLitigationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualAtCarryingValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5,800</ix:nonFraction>).</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i>Aphria Inc. Securities Litigation (New York, United States)</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 5, 2018,&#160;</em>a putative securities class action was commenced in SDNY against Aphria and certain current and former officers and directors. The action claims that the defendants misrepresented the value of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;cannabis-producing properties Aphria acquired in Jamaica, Colombia, and Argentina (the &#8220;LATAM Assets&#8221;). On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 3, 2018,&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">two</em>&#160;notorious short-sellers issued a report about the acquisitions, claiming the LATAM Assets were non-functional or non-existent, which allegedly caused Aphria&#8217;s stock price to fall. On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> April 15, 2019,&#160;</em>Aphria took impairment charges on the LATAM Assets, which also allegedly caused Aphria&#8217;s stock price to decline. The putative class action claims that Aphria artificially inflated the price of its publicly-traded stock by making false statements about the LATAM Assets, and, when the purported truth was revealed by a short-seller report and write-down, the stock price declined, harming investors.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2020,&#160;</em>the Court denied the motion to dismiss the complaint as to Aphria, Vic Neufeld, and Carl Merton, and granted the motion as to Cole Cacciavillani, John Cervini, Andrew DeFrancesco, and SOL Global Investments. On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> October 1, 2020,&#160;</em>Plaintiffs moved for reconsideration of the order dismissing DeFrancesco and SOL or, in the alternative, to amend their complaint. On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> October 14, 2020,&#160;</em>Aphria, Neufeld, and Merton moved for reconsideration of the order denying their motion to dismiss. On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 28, 2021,&#160;</em>the Court denied all motions for reconsideration and provided Plaintiffs with the opportunity to amend their complaint. Plaintiffs did&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;amend, and so the dismissals of Cacciavillani, Cervini, DeFrancesco, and SOL Investments became dismissals with prejudice.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 28, 2022,&#160;</em>Plaintiffs moved for class certification, and briefing on the motion was complete as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 28, 2022.&#160;</em>The motion was granted, and a class was certified. On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> April 12, 2024,&#160;</em>the parties filed a revised schedule for the remainder of the proceeding through trial. As of the date of this Form&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K, the parties have completed fact discovery. There is currently <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> court-ordered timetable in place for the litigation. The Company and the individual defendants believe the claims are without merit and will continue to vigorously defend against them, but there can be&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;assurances as to the outcome.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i>Dismissal of Martin Dionne suit v. HEXO Corporation and Sebastien St. Louis</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2019, </em>a Canadian securities class action was instituted against HEXO Corp. (&#8220;HEXO&#8221;) and its former CEO, Sebastien St. Louis. The plaintiff claims that between <em style="font: inherit;"> April 11, 2018 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> March 30, 2020, </em>the defendants misrepresented material facts, in both documents and oral statements and failed to disclose material changes in a timely manner as it relates to: (a) revenue certainty in the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> year post-legalization (<em style="font: inherit;">2018</em> supply agreement with the province of Qu&#233;bec); (b) additional revenue generation (acquisition of Newstrike); (c) HEXO inventory and internal controls; and (d) licensing at the Niagara facility.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> January 23, 2023, </em>the class action was dismissed in its entirety at the certification stage in Quebec. On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 14, 2023, </em>the plaintiff appealed this decision to the Quebec Court of Appeal. The appeal was heard on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 18, 2024 </em>and the Quebec Court of Appeal dismissed this appeal on <em style="font: inherit;"> April 16, 2025.&#160; </em>Following successful dismissal of plaintiff&#8217;s appeal, the Company intends to pursue recovery of D&amp;O policy retention amounts following the successful outcome.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b>Legal Proceedings Related to Contractual Obligations</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Settlement and Dismissal of <em style="font: inherit;">420</em></i></b>&#160;<b><i>Investments Ltd. Litigation</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 21, 2020,&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">420</em>&#160;Investments Ltd., as Plaintiff (<em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;420</em>&#160;Investments&#8221;), filed a lawsuit against Tilray Brands, Inc. and High Park Shops Inc. (&#8220;High Park&#8221;), as Defendants, in Calgary, Alberta in the Court of Queen&#8217;s Bench of Alberta. In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> August 2019,&#160;</em>Tilray and High Park entered into an Arrangement Agreement with&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">420</em>&#160;Investments and others (the &#8220;Agreement&#8221;). Pursuant to the Agreement, High Park was to acquire the securities of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">420</em>&#160;Investments. In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 2020,&#160;</em>Tilray and High Park gave notice of termination of the Agreement.&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">420</em>&#160;Investments alleged that the termination was unlawful and without merit.&#160; <em style="font: inherit;">420</em>&#160;Investments sought damages in the stated amount of CAD $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140439" contextRef="d_2020-02-21_2020-02-21_LitigationCaseAxis-The420InvestmentsLtdLitigationMember_LitigationStatusAxis-PendingLitigationMember_LossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis-DamagesMember" unitRef="CAD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyDamagesSoughtValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">110,000</ix:nonFraction>, plus&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140440">C$20,000</span>&#160;in aggravated damages. High Park subsequently counterclaimed against&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">420</em>&#160;Investments for repayment of a CAD $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140442" contextRef="i_2024-05-31_LitigationCaseAxis-TilrayAndHighParkVs420InvestmentsUnpaidDebtCollectionMember" unitRef="CAD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">7,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;bridge loan made to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">420</em>&#160;Investments in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> August 2019.&#160;</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 7, 2024,&#160;</em>the court granted summary judgment in favor of High Park on its counterclaim. The summary judgment order was equal to the amount of CAD $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140444" contextRef="i_2024-02-07_GainContingenciesByNatureAxis-PositiveOutcomeOfLitigationMember_LitigationCaseAxis-TilrayAndHighParkVs420InvestmentsUnpaidDebtCollectionMember" unitRef="CAD" name="us-gaap:NotesReceivableNet" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">7,000</ix:nonFraction>, plus pre-judgment interest in the amount of CAD $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140445" contextRef="i_2024-02-07_GainContingenciesByNatureAxis-PositiveOutcomeOfLitigationMember_LitigationCaseAxis-TilrayAndHighParkVs420InvestmentsUnpaidDebtCollectionMember" unitRef="CAD" name="us-gaap:InterestReceivable" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">2,280</ix:nonFraction>.&#160;On <em style="font: inherit;"> October 16, 2024, </em>the court subsequently overturned the summary judgment decision, and High Park subsequently appealed that decision.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 29, 2024,&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">420</em> Investments and others&#160;filed a Notice of Intention to Make a Proposal under subsection&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">50.4</em>(<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) of the&#160;Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act, RSC&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">1985,</em>&#160;c. B-<em style="font: inherit;">3.</em> On <em style="font: inherit;"> September 19, 2024, </em>the court directed <em style="font: inherit;">420</em> Investments to enter a strategic sales process under the <i>Companies</i>&#8217;<i> Creditors Arrangement Act</i>, RSC <em style="font: inherit;">1985,</em> c-<em style="font: inherit;">36.</em> In the course of the insolvency proceedings, Tilray purchased the claims of certain entities for a significant discount and with an aggregate approximate value of CAD $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140454" contextRef="d_2024-09-19_2024-09-19_GainContingenciesByNatureAxis-PositiveOutcomeOfLitigationMember_LitigationCaseAxis-TilrayAndHighParkVs420InvestmentsUnpaidDebtCollectionMember" unitRef="CAD" name="us-gaap:RepaymentsOfDebt" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1,400</ix:nonFraction>.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 11, 2025, </em>the parties successfully settled the <em style="font: inherit;">420</em> Investments proceedings. The terms of the settlement agreement, which were approved by the court, included payment by Tilray of a net amount equal to approximately <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140456">$2,700;</span> Tilray&#8217;s waiver of any recovery on its acquired claims; and the assignment back to <em style="font: inherit;">420</em> investments of the CAD $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140458" contextRef="i_2025-05-11_GainContingenciesByNatureAxis-PositiveOutcomeOfLitigationMember_LitigationCaseAxis-TilrayAndHighParkVs420InvestmentsUnpaidDebtCollectionMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:NotesReceivableNet" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">7,000</ix:nonFraction> bridge loan plus interest and costs.&#160; In exchange, <em style="font: inherit;">420</em> Investments&#8217; litigation claims were fully dismissed and the parties executed mutual releases.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Fotmer Corporation S.A. v. Tilray Brands Inc. et al.</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> January 4, 2023, </em>Fotmer Corporation S.A. commenced an arbitration demanding $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140460" contextRef="d_2023-01-04_2023-01-04_LitigationCaseAxis-FotmerCorporationSaVTilrayBrandsIncEtAlMember_LitigationStatusAxis-SettledLitigationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyDamagesSoughtValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,233</ix:nonFraction>&#160;for alleged breaches by Tilray of a <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> purchase agreement. On <em style="font: inherit;"> July 5, 2023, </em>Tilray responded by filing a court action in the Berlin Regional Court seeking $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140462" contextRef="d_2023-07-05_2023-07-05_LitigationCaseAxis-FotmerCorporationSaVTilrayBrandsIncEtAlMember_LitigationStatusAxis-SettledLitigationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyDamagesSoughtValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">2,250</ix:nonFraction>&#160;under a <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> supply agreement asserting that Fotmer&#8217;s alleged monetary claims under the <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> supply agreements are improper, and that Fotmer owes Tilray $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140466" contextRef="i_2023-07-05_LitigationCaseAxis-FotmerCorporationSaVTilrayBrandsIncEtAlMember_LitigationStatusAxis-SettledLitigationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyReceivableNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">2.25</ix:nonFraction> million in respect of advance payments made for future deliveries and certain reimbursement obligations owing by Fotmer to Tilray for defective products and EU GMP certifications.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> August 8, 2023, </em>a final award was issued in the arbitration between the parties, ordering Tilray to pay Fotmer damages in the amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140467" contextRef="d_2023-08-08_2023-08-08_LitigationCaseAxis-FotmerCorporationSaVTilrayBrandsIncEtAlMember_LitigationStatusAxis-SettledLitigationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyDamagesAwardedValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,233</ix:nonFraction>, plus simple interest of <ix:nonFraction id="c131140468" contextRef="d_2023-08-08_2023-08-08_LitigationCaseAxis-FotmerCorporationSaVTilrayBrandsIncEtAlMember_LitigationStatusAxis-SettledLitigationMember" unitRef="Pure" name="tlry:LossContingencyDamagesAwardedInterestFeePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">7.5</ix:nonFraction>% from <em style="font: inherit;"> December 29, 2020 </em>forward, in connection with the <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> supply agreement.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Tilray has yet to pay Fotmer any amounts owed pursuant to the arbitral award on the basis that the facts and legal issues in the court action and the arbitration overlap, such that equitable setoff should be applied between the <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> proceedings. In the court action, Fotmer submitted its statement of defense on <em style="font: inherit;"> November 7, 2023. </em>On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 21, 2024, </em>Tilray filed its statement of reply and defense against counterclaims.&#160;Tilray believes that Fotmer&#8217;s claims are without merit and the Company intends to vigorously defend against these claims.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Summary of litigation accruals</b>&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt; text-align: justify;">As described in Note&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">15</em>&#160;(Accounts payable and accrued liabilities), the total estimated litigation&#160;expense accrual included in accrued liabilities as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>&#160;was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c131140472" contextRef="i_2025-05-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualAtCarryingValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">12,431</ix:nonFraction>&#160;(<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2024&#160;- $</em><ix:nonFraction id="c131140473" contextRef="i_2024-05-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualAtCarryingValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">24,378</ix:nonFraction>). This estimated accrual is intended to cover various ongoing litigation matters with probable losses that can be reasonably estimated. The Company did&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140474">not</span>&#160;assume any litigation accruals from the Craft Acquisition II.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Financial instruments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company has classified its financial instruments as described in Note <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> (Significant accounting policies<i>)</i>.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The carrying values of marketable securities, accounts receivable, bank indebtedness and accounts payable and accrued liabilities approximate their fair values due to their short periods to maturity.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2024, </em>the Company had long-term debt of $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140478" contextRef="i_2025-05-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-LongtermDebtExcludingConvertibleDebenturesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LongtermDebtPercentageBearingFixedInterestAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">2,546</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140479" contextRef="i_2024-05-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-LongtermDebtExcludingConvertibleDebenturesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LongtermDebtPercentageBearingFixedInterestAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">3,568</ix:nonFraction>, respectively,&#160;and the principal portion of convertible debentures payable of $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140480" contextRef="i_2025-05-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-ConvertibleDebtMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ConvertibleDebt" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">105,00</ix:nonFraction> and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c131140481" contextRef="i_2024-05-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-ConvertibleDebtMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ConvertibleDebt" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">172,830</ix:nonFraction>, respectively,&#160;subject to fixed interest rates.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Fair value hierarchy</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Financial instruments recorded at fair value are classified using a fair value hierarchy that reflects the significance of inputs used in making the measurements. Cash and cash equivalents are Level <em style="font: inherit;">1.</em> The hierarchy is summarized as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 63pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets and liabilities</p> </td></tr>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company&#8217;s financial assets and liabilities required to be measured on a recurring basis are its convertible notes receivable, equity investments measured at fair value, convertible debentures measured at fair value, acquisition-related contingent consideration, and warrant liability.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Convertible notes receivable and long-term investments are recorded at fair value. The estimated fair value is determined by assessing&#160;the collateral entitlement from the asset and is classified as Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">3.</em>&#160;During the fiscal year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025,&#160;</em>an&#160;impairment to convertible notes receivable of $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140490" contextRef="d_2024-06-01_2025-05-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesFvNiUnrealizedGainLoss" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">21,661</ix:nonFraction> was recognized, compared to an impairment of $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140491" contextRef="d_2023-06-01_2024-05-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesFvNiUnrealizedGainLoss" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">42,681</ix:nonFraction> in the fiscal year ended&#160;&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31,&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2024.</em>&#160;Subsequent to the impairment recorded in <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2025,&#160;</em>MedMen exited receivership and substantially all of its remaining assets were transferred to a new entity owned by MedMen&#8217;s secured creditors, including SH Acquisition. In connection with the foregoing, the Company disposed&#160;of its MedMen Convertible Note in exchange for on option to acquire a&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c131140493" contextRef="i_2025-05-31_OwnershipAxis-SuperheroAcquisitionLPMember_StatementScenarioAxis-UponUsFederalCannabisLegalizationMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:MinorityInterestOwnershipPercentageByParent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">68</ix:nonFraction>% membership interest in&#160;SH Acquisition&#160;for $<ix:nonFraction id="c131140494" contextRef="i_2025-05-31_OwnershipAxis-SuperheroAcquisitionLPMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="tlry:EquityInvestmentStrikePrice" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1.00</ix:nonFraction>&#160;upon U.S. federal cannabis legalization. See Note&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">9</em>&#160;(Long-term investments). This option was recorded as a Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>&#160;equity investment measured at fair value of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c131140497" contextRef="i_2025-05-31_OwnershipAxis-SuperheroAcquisitionLPMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesWithoutReadilyDeterminableFairValueAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">8,160</ix:nonFraction> by assessing the discounted cash flows of&#160;SH Acquisition.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Convertible debentures payable are recorded at fair value when elected or required under US GAAP. Specifically, the APHA&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">24</em>&#160;instrument's estimated fair value was&#160;determined using the Black-Scholes option pricing model and was&#160;classified as Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">3.</em> There is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> remaining principal balance outstanding of the APHA <em style="font: inherit;">24</em> notes as of <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025.&#160;</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Certain equity investments recorded at fair value have quoted prices in active markets for identical assets and are classified as Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">1.</em>&#160;The&#160;Company classified securities with observable inputs as Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>&#160;and without a quoted market price as Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">3.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The warrants associated with the warrant liability are classified as Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>&#160;derivatives. Consequently, the estimated fair value of the warrant liability is determined using the Black-Scholes pricing model. Until the warrants are exercised, expire, or other facts and circumstances lead the warrant liability to be reclassified to stockholders&#8217; equity, the warrant liability (which relates to warrants to purchase shares of Common Stock) is marked-to-market each reporting period with the change in fair value recorded as the&#160;change in fair value of warrant liability within the consolidated statements of loss and comprehensive loss. Any significant adjustments to the unobservable inputs disclosed in the table below would have a direct impact on the fair value of the warrant liability.</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Items measured at fair value on a non-recurring basis</span></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company's prepayments and other current assets, long-lived assets, including property and equipment, goodwill and intangible assets are measured at fair value when there is an indicator of impairment and are recorded at fair value only when an impairment charge is recognized.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Financial risk management</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company has exposure to the following risks from its use of financial instruments: credit; liquidity; currency rate; interest rate price; equity price risk; and capital management risk.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:2.8%;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:2.8%;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>(a)</i></p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:auto;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Credit risk</i></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Credit risk is the risk of financial loss to the Company if a customer or counterparty to a financial instrument fails to meet its contractual obligations. The maximum credit exposure at <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>, is the carrying amount of cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable, prepaids and other current assets and convertible notes receivable. All cash and cash equivalents are placed with major financial institutions in Canada, Australia, Portugal, Germany, Colombia, Argentina and the United States.<b> </b>To date, the Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> experienced any losses on its cash deposits. Accounts receivable are unsecured, and the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> require collateral from its customers.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company evaluates the collectability of its accounts receivable and maintains an allowance for credit losses at an amount sufficient to absorb losses inherent in the existing accounts receivable portfolio as of the reporting dates based on the estimate of expected net credit losses.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>, the Company&#8217;s financial liabilities consisted of bank indebtedness and accounts payable and accrued liabilities, which have contractual maturity dates within <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-year, as well as long-term debt&#160;and convertible debentures which have contractual maturities over the next <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> years.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company maintains a minimum deposit on certain&#160;cash operating accounts tied to loans secured by its Aphria One,&#160;SweetWater, and craft beverage facilities. The Company maintains debt service charge and leverage covenants on certain loans secured by its Aphria Diamond facilities and ABC Group&#160;that are measured quarterly.&#160;&#160;The Company believes that it has sufficient operating room with respect to its financial covenants for the next fiscal year and does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> anticipate being in breach of any of its financial covenants.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company manages its liquidity risk by reviewing its capital requirements on an ongoing basis. Based on the Company&#8217;s working capital position as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>, management regards liquidity risk to be low.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:2.8%;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:2.8%;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>(c)</i></p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:auto;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Currency rate risk</i></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2025</em>, a portion of the Company&#8217;s financial assets and liabilities held in Canadian dollars and Euros consist of cash and cash equivalents, convertible notes receivable, and long-term investments. The Company&#8217;s objective in managing its foreign currency risk is to minimize its net exposure to foreign currency cash flows by transacting, to the greatest extent possible, with <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties in the functional currency. The Company is exposed to currency rate risk in other comprehensive income, relating to foreign subsidiaries which operate in a foreign currency. The Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> currently use foreign exchange contracts to hedge its exposure to its foreign currency cash flows as management has determined that this risk is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> significant at this point in time.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company&#8217;s exposure to changes in interest rates relate&#160;primarily to the Company&#8217;s outstanding debt. The Company manages interest rate risk by restricting the type of investments and varying the terms of maturity and issuers of marketable securities. Varying the terms to maturity reduces the sensitivity of the portfolio to the impact of interest rate fluctuations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:2.8%;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:2.8%;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>(e)</i></p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:auto;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Capital management</i></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company&#8217;s objectives when managing its capital are to safeguard its ability to continue as a going concern, to meet its capital expenditures for its continued operations, and to maintain a flexible capital structure which optimizes the cost of capital within a framework of acceptable risk. The Company manages its capital structure and adjusts it in light of changes in economic conditions and the risk characteristics of the underlying assets. To maintain or adjust its capital structure, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue new shares, issue new debt, or acquire or dispose of assets. The Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to externally imposed capital requirements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Management reviews its capital management approach on an ongoing basis and believes that this approach, given the relative size of the Company, is reasonable. There have been <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> changes to the Company&#8217;s capital management approach in the year. The Company considers its cash and cash equivalents and marketable securities as capital.</p>

</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Our Company&#8217;s Chief Operating Decision Maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;) is the Chairman of the Board of Directors and Chief Executive Officer. The&#160;CODM uses segment gross profit for the purpose of resource allocation, assessment of segment performance against determined targets, and in deciding whether to implement cost saving targets. The Company operates in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c131140540">four</span> segments. <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) cannabis operations, which encompasses the production, distribution,&#160;sale, co-manufacturing and advisory services of both medical and adult-use cannabis, <em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) beverage operations, which encompasses the production, marketing and sale of beverage products, <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>) distribution operations, which encompasses the purchase and resale of pharmaceuticals products to customers, and <em style="font: inherit;">4</em>) wellness products, which encompasses hemp foods and cannabidiol (&#8220;CBD&#8221;) products. This structure is in line with how our CODM assesses our performance and allocates resources.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Operating segments have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been aggregated and <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> asset information is provided for the segments because the Company&#8217;s CODM does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> receive asset information by segment on a regular basis.&#160;</p>

  <div><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><a id="report" title="report" href="#"></a>REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</b></p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">To the Board of Directors and Shareholders of Tilray Brands, Inc.</p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Opinions on the Financial Statements and Internal Control over Financial Reporting</b></p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated statements of financial position of Tilray Brands, Inc. and its subsidiaries (together, the Company) as of May 31, 2025 and 2024, and the related consolidated statements of loss and comprehensive loss, of changes in equity and of cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended May 31, 2025, including the related notes (collectively referred to as the consolidated financial statements). We also have audited the Company's internal control over financial reporting as of May 31, 2025, based on criteria established in <i>Internal Control &#8211; Integrated Framework (2013) </i>issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO).</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of May 31, 2025 and 2024, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended May 31, 2025 in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. Also in our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of May 31, 2025, based on criteria established in<i> Internal Control &#8211; Integrated Framework (2013)</i> issued by the COSO.</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Basis for Opinions</b></p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company&#8217;s management is responsible for these consolidated financial statements, for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting, and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting appearing under Item 9A. Our responsibility is to express opinions on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements and on the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting based on our audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United&#160;States) (PCAOB) and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audits to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the consolidated financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud, and whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects.</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Our audits of the consolidated financial statements included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the consolidated financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the consolidated financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the consolidated financial statements. Our audit of internal control over financial reporting included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk. Our audits also included performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinions.</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">As described in Management's Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting, management has excluded the acquired craft beer brands and breweries from Molson Coors Beverage Company which include Atwater Brewery, Hop Valley Brewing Company, Terrapin Beer Co., and Revolver Brewing (the Craft Acquisition II) from its assessment of internal control over financial reporting as of May 31, 2025, because they were acquired by the Company in purchase business combinations during the year ended May 31, 2025. The Craft Acquisition II are wholly-owned subsidiaries whose total assets and total revenues excluded from management&#8217;s assessment and our audit of internal control over financial reporting represent 0.9% of total assets and 3% of net revenues, respectively, of the related consolidated financial statement amounts as of and for the year ended May 31, 2025.</p>
